title.en: Volume 131 Biographies 19: Gu Shi, Wu Zhen, Xue Xian, Guo Xing, Chen De, Wang Zhi, Mei Sizu, Jin Chaoxing, Tang Shengzong, Lu Zhongheng, Fei Ju, Lu Ju, Zheng Yuchun, Huang Bin, Ye Sheng
title.raw: 卷一百三十一 列傳第十九 顧時 吳楨 薛顯 郭興 陳德 王志 梅思祖 金朝興 唐勝宗 陸仲亨 費聚 陸聚 鄭遇春 黃彬 葉昇 Volume 131 Biographies 19: Gu Shi, Wu Zhen, Xue Xian, Guo Xing, Chen De, Wang Zhi, Mei Sizu, Jin Chaoxing, Tang Shengzong, Lu Zhongheng, Fei Ju, Lu Ju, Zheng Yuchun, Huang Bin, Ye Sheng

sentences.zh: 顧時，字時舉，濠人。

translations.literal: Gu Shi, styled Shiju, was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shi, whose courtesy name was Shiju, came from Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 倜儻好奇略。

translations.literal: He was unrestrained and fond of bold stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and unconventional, he delighted in daring schemes.

sentences.zh: 從太祖渡江，積功由百夫長授元帥。

translations.literal: Following the Taizu in crossing the Yangzi, through accumulated merit he rose from centurion to be appointed marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi with Taizu and, rising on merit, advanced from centurion to marshal.

sentences.zh: 取安慶、南昌、廬州、泰州，擢天策衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: He took Anqing, Nanchang, Luzhou, and Taizhou, and was promoted to vice commander of the Tiance Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Anqing, Nanchang, Luzhou, and Taizhou, he was promoted to vice commander of the Tiance Guard.

sentences.zh: 李濟據濠州，時從平章韓政討降之。

translations.literal: Li Ji held Haozhou; Shi followed the Pacification Commissioner Han Zheng to attack and subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ji held Haozhou, Gu Shi joined Pacification Commissioner Han Zheng in the campaign to reduce him.

sentences.zh: 攻張士誠升山水寨，引小舫繞敵舟，舟中多俯視而笑。

translations.literal: Attacking Zhang Shicheng's Shengshan stockade, he led small boats around the enemy vessels; many aboard looked down and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Zhang Shicheng's Shengshan river fort, he sent small boats skirting the enemy fleet, and many on the enemy ships leaned over the rails to laugh.

sentences.zh: 時乘其懈，帥壯士數人，大呼躍入舟。

translations.literal: Shi seized their slackness, led several stalwarts, and with a great shout leaped into their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shi seized their negligence, took a handful of stalwarts, and with a shout leaped aboard.

sentences.zh: 眾大亂，余舟競進。

translations.literal: The masses fell into great disorder, and the remaining boats raced forward.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy ranks broke in chaos, and the rest of the fleet pressed in at once.

sentences.zh: 五太子來援，薛顯又敗之，五太子等降。

translations.literal: The Fifth Prince came to relieve them; Xue Xian again defeated him, and the Fifth Prince and others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fifth Prince came to the rescue, Xue Xian defeated him again, and the Fifth Prince and his force surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂從大將軍平吳，旋師取山東。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed the grand general to pacify Wu, then turned the army to take Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched with the grand general to pacify Wu, and afterward turned his columns toward Shandong.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，拜大都督府副使兼同知率府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was appointed deputy commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and concurrently vice director of the Staff Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 (1368), he was made deputy commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and concurrently vice director of the Staff Office.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍定河南北，浚閘以通舟師，自臨清至通州。

translations.literal: He followed the grand general in pacifying the north and south of the Yellow River, dredged locks to open passage for the fleet, from Linqing to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the grand general in pacifying the regions north and south of the Yellow River, dredged the locks to open the water route for the fleet from Linqing to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 下元都，與諸將分邏古北諸隘口。

translations.literal: He took the Yuan capital and, with the various generals, divided among themselves the passes of the Gubeikou region.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Yuan capital, he and the other generals divided the Gubeikou passes among themselves.

sentences.zh: 從大軍取平陽，克崞州，獲逃將王信等四十六人。

translations.literal: Following the main army he took Pingyang, captured Guozhou, and seized the fugitive generals Wang Xin and forty-five others.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with the main army to take Pingyang, captured Guozhou, and seized forty-six fugitive officers including the general Wang Xin.

sentences.zh: 取蘭州，圍慶陽。

translations.literal: He took Lanzhou and besieged Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Lanzhou and laid siege to Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 張良臣耀兵城下，擊敗之，獲其勁將九人。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangchen displayed his troops below the city; Shi defeated him and captured nine of his crack generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liangchen paraded his troops before the walls, Gu Shi routed him and took nine of his best generals prisoner.

sentences.zh: 良臣乃不敢復出。

translations.literal: Liangchen then dared not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: After that Zhang Liangchen did not dare sally forth again.

sentences.zh: 慶陽平。

translations.literal: Qingyang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 徐達還京，令時將騎兵略靜寧州，走賀宗哲。

translations.literal: Xu Da returned to the capital and ordered Shi to lead cavalry in a sweep of Jingning Prefecture, putting He Zongzhe to flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da returned to the capital, he ordered Gu Shi to lead the cavalry in a sweep of Jingning and drive off He Zongzhe.

sentences.zh: 西邊悉平。

translations.literal: The western frontier was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier was brought entirely to order.

sentences.zh: 三年進大都督同知，封濟寧侯，祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to associate commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jining with an emolument of fifteen hundred piculs, and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to associate commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jining with fifteen hundred piculs of grain, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 四年為左副將軍，副傅友德帥河南、陝西步騎伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he served as left deputy general, assisting Fu Youde in commanding the infantry and cavalry of Henan and Shaanxi to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became left deputy general and seconded Fu Youde in leading the infantry and cavalry of Henan and Shaanxi against Shu.

sentences.zh: 自興元進克階、文，敗蜀兵於漢州，遂克成都。

translations.literal: Advancing from Xingyuan he captured Jie and Wen, defeated the Shu army at Hanzhou, and thereupon took Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing from Xingyuan, he took Jie and Wen, routed the Shu forces at Hanzhou, and then captured Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 明年副李文忠北征，分道入沙漠。

translations.literal: The next year he assisted Li Wenzhong on the northern expedition, entering the desert by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he seconded Li Wenzhong on the northern campaign, and their columns entered the desert by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 迷失道，糧且盡。

translations.literal: They lost their way, and provisions were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They lost their way, and their provisions were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 遇寇，士疲不能戰。

translations.literal: They encountered bandits; the troops were weary and unable to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When they met the enemy, the men were too exhausted to give battle.

sentences.zh: 時帥麾下數百人，躍馬衝擊。

translations.literal: Shi led several hundred men under his command, leaped on his horse, and charged.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shi led several hundred of his own men, spurred his horse forward, and charged the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵眾引去，獲其輜重糧畜以歸，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: The enemy masses withdrew; he seized their baggage, grain, and livestock and returned, and the army's renown greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew; he seized their baggage train, grain, and livestock and returned, and the army's morale soared.

sentences.zh: 六年從徐達鎮北平。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召還。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 八年復出鎮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again went out to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned to the frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 葬鐘山。

translations.literal: He was buried on Bell Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on Bell Mountain.

sentences.zh: 追封滕國公，諡襄靖，祔祭功臣廟。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng, with the posthumous title Xiangjing, and enshrined for sacrifice in the Temple of Meritorious Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Teng with the temple name Xiangjing, and his tablet was placed in the Temple of Meritorious Officials.

sentences.zh: 時能以少擊眾，沉鷙不伐。

translations.literal: Shi was able to strike the many with the few; deep and reserved, he did not boast.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shi could rout larger forces with smaller numbers; reserved and self-contained, he never boasted of his deeds.

sentences.zh: 帝甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 子敬，金吾衛鎮撫，十五年嗣侯，為左副將軍。

translations.literal: His son Jing was garrison commander of the Jinyu Guard; in the fifteenth year he succeeded to the marquisate and served as left deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, garrison commander of the Jinyu Guard, succeeded to the marquisate in the fifteenth year and served as left deputy general.

sentences.zh: 平龍泉山寇有功。

translations.literal: He had merit in pacifying the bandits of Longquan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in suppressing the bandits of Longquan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 二十三年追論胡惟庸黨，榜列諸臣，以時為首，敬坐死，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, in a retrospective prosecution of the Hu Weiyong faction, a public list named the ministers; Shi was placed first; Jing was sentenced to death, and the nobility was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, when the Hu Weiyong faction was prosecuted retroactively, a public list of implicated ministers placed Gu Shi at the head; Jing was executed, and the marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 吳禎，江國襄烈公良弟也。

translations.literal: Wu Zhen was the younger brother of Liang, Duke of Jiang with the posthumous title Xianglie.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen was the younger brother of Wu Liang, Duke of Jiang, posthumously titled Xianglie.

sentences.zh: 初名國寶，賜名禎。

translations.literal: His original name was Guobao; he was granted the name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Guobao; the throne granted him the name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 與良俱從克滁、和，渡江克採石，從定集慶。

translations.literal: Together with Liang he followed in capturing Chuzhou and Hezhou, crossed the Yangzi and took Caishi, and followed in pacifying Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liang followed the campaigns that took Chuzhou and Hezhou, crossed the Yangzi to capture Caishi, and helped secure Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 下鎮江、廣德、常州、宣城、江陰，皆有功。

translations.literal: In reducing Zhenjiang, Guangde, Changzhou, Xuancheng, and Jiangyin he had merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the reduction of Zhenjiang, Guangde, Changzhou, Xuancheng, and Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 又從常遇春自銅陵取池州，以舟師毀其北門，入城。

translations.literal: Again he followed Chang Yuchun from Tongling to take Chizhou; with the fleet he destroyed the north gate and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Chang Yuchun from Tongling to take Chizhou, where the fleet breached the north gate and entered the city.

sentences.zh: 敵艦百余至，復大敗之，遂克池州。

translations.literal: More than a hundred enemy ships arrived; he again inflicted a great defeat and thereupon captured Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a hundred enemy ships arrived, he routed them again and took Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 積功，由帳前都先鋒累遷為天興翼副元帥。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he rose from vanguard commander before the tent by successive promotions to deputy marshal of the Tianxing Wing.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he rose from vanguard commander in the imperial guard to deputy marshal of the Tianxing Wing.

sentences.zh: 以千人助良守江陰，數敗吳兵，破士誠水寨，擒其驍將硃定。

translations.literal: With a thousand men he assisted Liang in defending Jiangyin, repeatedly defeated the Wu troops, broke Zhang Shicheng's river stockade, and captured his fierce general Zhu Ding.
translations.idiomatic: With a thousand men he helped Liang hold Jiangyin, repeatedly defeated the Wu forces, broke Zhang Shicheng's river stockade, and captured his crack general Zhu Ding.

sentences.zh: 授英武衛親軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of the personal guard of the Yingwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of the personal guard of the Yingwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 又大破吳兵於浮子門。

translations.literal: Again he inflicted a great defeat on the Wu troops at Fuzi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed the Wu forces at Fuzi Gate.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍徐達帥馬步舟師取湖州，勒奇兵出舊館，大捷。

translations.literal: He followed the grand general Xu Da in commanding horse, foot, and fleet to take Huzhou; he led elite troops out from Jiuguan and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Xu Da in leading horse, foot, and fleet against Huzhou, sent elite troops out from Jiuguan, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 湖州平，遂戍之。

translations.literal: Huzhou was pacified, and he then garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: After Huzhou was pacified, he garrisoned the city.

sentences.zh: 從圍平江，破葑、胥二門，進僉大都督府事，撫平江。

translations.literal: He followed in besieging Pingjiang, broke the Fu and Xu gates, was advanced to commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, and pacified Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the siege of Pingjiang, breached the Fu and Xu gates, was promoted to commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, and pacified the city.

sentences.zh: 尋副征南將軍湯和討方國珍，乘潮入曹娥江，毀壩通道，出不意直抵軍廄。

translations.literal: Soon he assisted the southern expedition general Tang He in campaigning against Fang Guozhen; riding the tide he entered the Cao'e River, destroyed the dam to open a passage, and by surprise went straight to the army stables.
translations.idiomatic: He soon seconded Southern Expedition General Tang He against Fang Guozhen, entered the Cao'e River on the tide, breached the dam to open a channel, and by surprise struck straight at the enemy encampment.

sentences.zh: 國珍亡入海。

translations.literal: Guozhen fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 追及之盤嶼，合戰，自申至戌，敗之，盡獲其戰艦士卒輜重，國珍降。

translations.literal: Pursuing him to Pan Isle, they joined battle from the shen hour to the xu hour, defeated him, and captured all his warships, troops, and baggage; Guozhen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They overtook him at Pan Isle and fought from mid-afternoon until evening; he was defeated, and they seized his entire fleet, army, and baggage train before Fang Guozhen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復自海道進取福州，圍其西、南、水部三門，一鼓克之。

translations.literal: Again by the sea route he advanced to take Fuzhou, besieged its west, south, and water gates, and took it in one assault.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced again by sea to take Fuzhou, invested the west, south, and water gates, and captured the city in a single assault.

sentences.zh: 十一年，奉詔出定遼，得疾，輿還京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, by imperial order he went out to pacify Liaodong; he fell ill and was carried back to the capital in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was ordered to pacify Liaodong; he fell ill and was carried back to the capital in a litter.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 追封海國公，諡襄毅，與良俱肖像功臣廟。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hai, with the posthumous title Xiangyi; together with Liang their portraits were placed in the Temple of Meritorious Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Hai with the temple name Xiangyi, and his portrait was placed in the Temple of Meritorious Officials alongside Liang's.

sentences.zh: 子忠嗣侯。

translations.literal: His son Zhong succeeded to the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 二十三年追論禎胡惟庸黨，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, in a retrospective prosecution of Zhen as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, the nobility was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, when Wu Zhen was prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, the marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 薛顯，蕭人。

translations.literal: Xue Xian was a man of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xian came from Xiao County.

sentences.zh: 趙均用據徐州，以顯為元帥，守泗州。

translations.literal: Zhao Junyong held Xuzhou and appointed Xian marshal to guard Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Junyong held Xuzhou, he appointed Xue Xian marshal and stationed him at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 均用死，以泗州來降，授親軍指揮，從征伐。

translations.literal: When Junyong died, he came with Sizhou to surrender; he was appointed commander of the personal guard and followed on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: After Junyong's death he surrendered Sizhou, was appointed commander of the personal guard, and took part in the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 南昌平，命顯從大都督硃文正守之。

translations.literal: When Nanchang was pacified, Xian was ordered to follow the chief commissioner Zhu Wenzheng in defending it.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanchang was pacified, he was ordered to serve under Chief Commissioner Zhu Wenzheng in its defense.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒寇南昌，顯守章江、新城二門。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang raided Nanchang; Xian defended the Zhangjiang and Xincheng gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang attacked Nanchang, Xue Xian held the Zhangjiang and Xincheng gates.

sentences.zh: 友諒攻甚急。

translations.literal: Youliang's assault was very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang pressed the assault fiercely.

sentences.zh: 顯隨方御之，間出銳卒搏戰，斬其平章劉進昭，擒副樞趙祥。

translations.literal: Xian defended as circumstances required; from time to time he sent out crack troops to grapple in battle, beheaded his Pacification Commissioner Liu Jinzhao, and captured Vice Director Zhao Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xian met each threat as it arose, and from time to time sent crack troops out to fight hand to hand; he slew the Pacification Commissioner Liu Jinzhao and captured Vice Director Zhao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 固守三月，乃解。

translations.literal: They held firm for three months before the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: After three months of stubborn defense the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 武昌既平，鄧仲謙據新淦不下，顯討斬之，因徇下未附諸郡縣。

translations.literal: After Wuchang was pacified, Deng Zhongqian held Xingan and would not submit; Xian campaigned against him and beheaded him, then in succession reduced the prefectures and counties that had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang fell, Deng Zhongqian held Xingan and refused to submit; Xue Xian campaigned against him, executed him, and then brought the remaining unsubdued prefectures and counties to heel.

sentences.zh: 以功擢江西行省參政。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to administrative commissioner of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was promoted to administrative commissioner of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從徐達等收淮東，遂伐張士誠。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da and others in recovering eastern Huai, then campaigned against Zhang Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da and others in recovering eastern Huai, then marched against Zhang Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 與常遇春攻湖州。

translations.literal: Together with Chang Yuchun he attacked Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Huzhou alongside Chang Yuchun.

sentences.zh: 別將游軍取德清，攻升山水寨。

translations.literal: As a separate commander he led mobile troops to take Deqing and attacked the Shengshan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: As a detached commander he led mobile columns to take Deqing and assaulted the Shengshan river fort.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣其五太子盛兵來援，遇春與戰，小卻。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent his Fifth Prince with a great army to relieve them; Yuchun joined battle and fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng sent his Fifth Prince with a large relief force; Chang Yuchun engaged them and was driven back slightly.

sentences.zh: 顯帥舟師奮擊，燒其船。

translations.literal: Xian led the fleet in a fierce assault and burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xian led the fleet in a fierce charge and burned the enemy ships.

sentences.zh: 眾大潰，五太子及硃暹、呂珍等以舊館降，得兵六萬人。

translations.literal: The masses broke in great rout; the Fifth Prince and Zhu Xian, Lü Zhen, and others surrendered at Jiuguan, and sixty thousand troops were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy army broke in rout; the Fifth Prince, Zhu Xian, Lü Zhen, and others surrendered at Jiuguan, yielding sixty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 遇春謂顯曰：「今日之戰，將軍功，遇春弗如也。

translations.literal: Yuchun said to Xian, "In today's battle the general's merit surpasses what Yuchun could have done."
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun told Xue Xian, "In today's battle the credit is yours; I am not your equal."

sentences.zh: 」五太子等既降，吳人震恐，湖州遂下。

translations.literal: After the Fifth Prince and others had surrendered, the Wu people were shaken with fear, and Huzhou was thereupon taken.
translations.idiomatic: After the Fifth Prince and his force surrendered, the Wu armies were shaken with fear, and Huzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 進圍平江，與諸將分門而軍。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Pingjiang, he and the various generals divided the gates among themselves and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Pingjiang, and he and the other generals divided the gates among themselves and encamped.

sentences.zh: 吳平，進行省右丞。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was advanced to right vice censor-in-chief of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 命從大將軍徐達取中原。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow the grand general Xu Da in taking the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to follow Grand General Xu Da in the conquest of the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，太祖諭諸將，謂「薛顯、傅友德勇略冠軍，可當一面。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, the Taizu instructed the generals, saying, "Xue Xian and Fu Youde in courage and stratagem lead the army; each can hold a front alone."
translations.idiomatic: Before they marched, Taizu told the generals, "In courage and strategy Xue Xian and Fu Youde are unmatched; either can hold a front on his own."

sentences.zh: 」進克兗、沂、青、濟，取東昌、棣州，樂安。

translations.literal: Advancing, he captured Yan, Yi, Qing, and Ji, and took Dongchang, Dizhou, and Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Yanzhou, Yizhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, and captured Dongchang, Dizhou, and Le'an.

sentences.zh: 還收河南，搗關、陝。

translations.literal: Returning, he recovered Henan and struck into Guan and Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned back to recover Henan and struck into the Guanzhong and Shaanxi regions.

sentences.zh: 渡河，取衛輝、彰德、廣平、臨清。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he took Weihui, Zhangde, Guangping, and Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yellow River and took Weihui, Zhangde, Guangping, and Linqing.

sentences.zh: 帥馬步舟師取德州、長蘆。

translations.literal: He commanded horse, foot, and fleet to take Dezhou and Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: He led horse, foot, and fleet to capture Dezhou and Changlu.

sentences.zh: 敗元兵於河西務，又敗之通州，遂克元都。

translations.literal: He defeated the Yuan troops at Hexiwu, again defeated them at Tongzhou, and thereupon captured the Yuan capital.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Yuan forces at Hexiwu, routed them again at Tongzhou, and then took the Yuan capital.

sentences.zh: 分兵邏古北諸隘口，略大同，獲喬右丞等三十四人。

translations.literal: He divided his forces among the passes of Gubeikou, swept Datong, and captured Right Chancellor Qiao and thirty-three others.
translations.idiomatic: He detached troops to the Gubeikou passes, raided Datong, and captured thirty-four men including Right Chancellor Qiao.

sentences.zh: 進征山西，次保定，取七垛寨，追敗脫因貼木兒。

translations.literal: Advancing to campaign in Shanxi, he halted at Baoding, took Qiduo Stockade, and in pursuit defeated Toqto'a.
translations.idiomatic: He marched into Shanxi, halted at Baoding, took Qiduo Stockade, and in pursuit defeated Toqto'a.

sentences.zh: 與友德將鐵騎三千，略平定西。

translations.literal: Together with Youde he led three thousand iron cavalry in a sweep of Pingding and Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: With Fu Youde he led three thousand armored horsemen in a sweep of Pingding and Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 取太原，走擴廓，降豁鼻馬。

translations.literal: He took Taiyuan, put Köke Temür to flight, and received the surrender of Huobima.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Taiyuan, drove off Köke Temür, and received the surrender of Huobima.

sentences.zh: 邀擊賀宗哲於石州，拔白崖、桃花諸山寨。

translations.literal: He intercepted and struck He Zongzhe at Shizhou and took the stockades of Baiya, Taohua, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He intercepted He Zongzhe at Shizhou and captured the mountain stockades at Baiya, Taohua, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 與大將軍達會平陽，以降將杜旺等十一人見，遂從入關中。

translations.literal: He joined the grand general Da at Pingyang, presented the surrendered generals Du Wang and ten others, and thereupon followed into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Grand General Xu Da at Pingyang, presented eleven surrendered generals including Du Wang, and then marched with him into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 抵臨洮，別將攻馬鞍山西番寨，大獲其畜產，襲走元豫王，敗擴廓於寧夏。

translations.literal: Reaching Lintao, as a separate commander he attacked the western barbarian stockades of Ma'anshan, seized a great quantity of their livestock, in a raid put the Yuan Prince of Yu to flight, and defeated Köke Temür at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: At Lintao he detached a column to attack the Tibetan stockades at Ma'anshan, seized large herds of livestock, drove off the Yuan Prince of Yu in a raid, and defeated Köke Temür at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 復與達會師取平涼。

translations.literal: Again he joined Da's army and took Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoined Xu Da's army and captured Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 張良臣偽以慶陽降，顯往納之。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangchen falsely offered to surrender Qingyang; Xian went to receive the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liangchen feigned surrender of Qingyang, Xue Xian went to accept it.

sentences.zh: 良臣蒲伏道迎，夜劫顯營，突圍免。

translations.literal: Liangchen lay in ambush along the road to welcome him; by night he raided Xian's camp; Xian broke through the encirclement and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen lay in ambush along the road to receive him, then raided Xue Xian's camp by night; Xue Xian broke through the encirclement and escaped.

sentences.zh: 良臣據城叛，達進圍之。

translations.literal: Liangchen held the city in rebellion; Da advanced to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liangchen seized the city and rebelled; Xu Da advanced to lay siege.

sentences.zh: 擴廓遣韓扎兒攻原州，以撓明師。

translations.literal: Köke Temür sent Han Zha'er to attack Yuanzhou to harass the Ming army.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür sent Han Zha'er to attack Yuanzhou in an attempt to relieve pressure on the Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 顯駐兵靈州，遏之。

translations.literal: Xian stationed troops at Lingzhou and checked them.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xian garrisoned Lingzhou and blocked their advance.

sentences.zh: 良臣援絕，遂敗。

translations.literal: Liangchen's relief was cut off, and he was thereupon defeated.
translations.idiomatic: With his relief cut off, Zhang Liangchen was defeated.

sentences.zh: 追賀宗哲於六盤山，逐擴廓出塞外，陝西悉平。

translations.literal: Pursuing He Zongzhe at Liupan Mountain, he drove Köke Temür beyond the frontier; Shaanxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued He Zongzhe to Liupan Mountain, drove Köke Temür beyond the frontier, and brought Shaanxi fully to order.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年冬，大封功臣。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Hongwu, the meritorious officials were greatly enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Hongwu 3 (1370), the throne enfeoffed the meritorious officials on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 以顯擅殺胥吏、獸醫、火者、馬軍及千戶吳富，面數其罪。

translations.literal: Because Xian had killed clerks, veterinarians, fire-keepers, cavalrymen, and the chiliarch Wu Fu on his own authority, the emperor confronted him and enumerated his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xue Xian had killed clerks, veterinarians, fire-keepers, cavalrymen, and the chiliarch Wu Fu on his own authority, the emperor confronted him and listed his crimes to his face.

sentences.zh: 封永城侯，勿予券，謫居海南。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng but was not granted a patent; he was banished to Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng but denied a hereditary patent and banished to Hainan.

sentences.zh: 分其祿為三：一以贍所殺吳富及馬軍之家；

translations.literal: His emolument was divided into three parts: one part to support the families of Wu Fu and the cavalrymen he had killed;
translations.idiomatic: His stipend was divided into three shares: one to support the families of Wu Fu and the cavalrymen he had killed;

sentences.zh: 一以給其母妻，令功過無相掩。

translations.literal: one part to provide for his mother and wife, so that merit and fault would not cover each other.
translations.idiomatic: one for his mother and wife, so that merit and fault would not cancel each other out.

sentences.zh: 顯居海南逾年，帝念之，召還。

translations.literal: After Xian had dwelt in Hainan for more than a year, the emperor thought of him and summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in Hainan, the emperor recalled him.

sentences.zh: 予世券，食祿一千五百石。

translations.literal: He was granted a hereditary patent and an emolument of fifteen hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He received a hereditary patent and a stipend of fifteen hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 復從大將軍征漠北。

translations.literal: Again he followed the grand general on campaigns in the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the grand general on campaigns beyond the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 數奉命巡視河南，屯田北平，練軍山西，從魏國公巡北邊，從宋國公出金山。

translations.literal: Repeatedly by imperial order he inspected Henan, garrisoned and farmed in Beiping, trained troops in Shanxi, followed the Duke of Wei on patrols of the northern border, and followed the Duke of Song out to Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered to inspect Henan, establish garrison farms in Beiping, drill troops in Shanxi, patrol the northern frontier with the Duke of Wei, and march to Jinshan with the Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 二十年冬，召還，次山海衛，卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twentieth year he was summoned back; he halted at Shanhai Guard and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twentieth year he was recalled; he died at Shanhai Guard on the way home.

sentences.zh: 贈永國公，諡桓襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yong with the posthumous title Huanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yong with the temple name Huanxiang.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟綱幼。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Gang was still young.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; his younger brother Gang was still a child.

sentences.zh: 二十三年追坐顯胡惟庸黨，以死不問，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was prosecuted retroactively as a member of Xian's Hu Weiyong faction; because he was already dead he was not punished, but the nobility was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was prosecuted retroactively as a member of Xue Xian's Hu Weiyong faction; because he was already dead he was not punished, but the marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 郭興，一名子興，濠人。

translations.literal: Guo Xing, also named Zixing, was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xing, also known as Zixing, came from Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 滁陽王郭子興據濠，稱元帥，與隸麾下。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chuyang, Guo Zixing, held Hao and styled himself marshal; Xing served under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Chuyang, Guo Zixing, held Haozhou and styled himself marshal, Guo Xing served in his ranks.

sentences.zh: 太祖在甥館，興歸心焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu was in the prince's household as a son-in-law; Xing gave him his loyal heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was a son-in-law in Guo Zixing's household, Guo Xing gave him his loyal allegiance.

sentences.zh: 軍行，嘗備宿衛，累功授管軍總管，進統軍元帥。

translations.literal: On campaign he often served as night guard; through accumulated merit he was appointed chief of army management and advanced to marshal commanding the army.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he often stood night guard; through accumulated merit he became chief of army management and was promoted to marshal commanding the army.

sentences.zh: 圍常州，晝夜不解甲者七月。

translations.literal: Besieging Changzhou, for seven months he did not remove his armor day or night.
translations.idiomatic: During the seven-month siege of Changzhou he never removed his armor, day or night.

sentences.zh: 城下，受上賞。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he received a superior reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he received a superior reward.

sentences.zh: 從攻寧國、江陰、宜興、婺州、安慶、衢州，皆下之。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Ningguo, Jiangyin, Yixing, Wuzhou, Anqing, and Quzhou; all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the attacks on Ningguo, Jiangyin, Yixing, Wuzhou, Anqing, and Quzhou, and all fell.

sentences.zh: 戰於鄱陽，陳友諒連巨艦以進，我師屢卻，興獻計以火攻之。

translations.literal: Fighting at Poyang, Chen Youliang advanced with great ships in succession; our army repeatedly fell back; Xing offered a plan to attack them with fire.
translations.idiomatic: At Poyang, Chen Youliang advanced in succession with huge ships; our forces were repeatedly driven back until Guo Xing proposed a fire attack.

sentences.zh: 友諒死。

translations.literal: Youliang died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang was killed.

sentences.zh: 從征武昌，斬獲多，進鷹揚衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Wuchang, he made many beheadings and captures and was advanced to commander of the Yingyang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the Wuchang campaign he took many heads and prisoners and was promoted to commander of the Yingyang Guard.

sentences.zh: 從徐達取廬州，援安豐，大敗張士誠兵。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking Luzhou, relieved Anfeng, and inflicted a great defeat on Zhang Shicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in taking Luzhou, relieved Anfeng, and routed Zhang Shicheng's army.

sentences.zh: 平襄陽、衡、澧。

translations.literal: He pacified Xiangyang, Hengzhou, and Li.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Xiangyang, Hengzhou, and Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還克高郵、淮安。

translations.literal: Returning, he captured Gaoyou and Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he captured Gaoyou and Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 轉戰湖州，圍平江，軍於婁門。

translations.literal: He fought at Huzhou, besieged Pingjiang, and encamped at the Lou Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Huzhou, besieged Pingjiang, and encamped at the Lou Gate.

sentences.zh: 吳平，擢鎮國將軍、大都督府僉事。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the State and commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the State and commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 三年為秦王武傅，兼陝西行都督府僉事。

translations.literal: In the third year he became military tutor to the Prince of Qin and concurrently commissioner of the Shaanxi Branch Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became military tutor to the Prince of Qin and concurrently commissioner of the Shaanxi Branch Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 其冬，封功臣，興以不守紀律，止封鞏昌侯，食祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: That winter, when the meritorious officials were enfeoffed, because Xing had not observed discipline he was only enfeoffed as Marquis of Gongchang with an emolument of fifteen hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the meritorious officials were enfeoffed, Guo Xing received only the marquisate of Gongchang with fifteen hundred piculs because he had not kept discipline; he was granted a hereditary patent nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 四年伐蜀，克漢州、成都。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he campaigned against Shu and captured Hanzhou and Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he campaigned against Shu and captured Hanzhou and Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 六年從徐達鎮北平，同陳德敗元兵於答刺海口。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping and, together with Chen De, defeated Yuan troops at Dalahaikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping and, with Chen De, defeated Yuan forces at Dalahaikou.

sentences.zh: 十一年練兵臨清。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he trained troops at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he drilled troops at Linqing.

sentences.zh: 十六年巡北邊。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he patrolled the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he patrolled the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 召還，逾年卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned back and died the following year.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and died the following year.

sentences.zh: 贈陝國公，諡宣武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Shaan with the posthumous title Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Shaan with the temple name Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 二十三年追坐胡惟庸黨，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, and the nobility was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, and the marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 興女弟為寧妃，弟英武定侯。

translations.literal: Xing's younger sister became Consort Ning; his younger brother was Marquis of Yingwu Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xing's younger sister became Consort Ning; his younger brother was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingwu Ding.

sentences.zh: 季弟德成，性通敏，嗜酒。

translations.literal: The youngest brother Decheng was quick and perceptive by nature and fond of wine.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Decheng was quick-witted by nature and fond of drink.

sentences.zh: 兩兄積功至列侯，而德成止驍騎舍人。

translations.literal: Both elder brothers through accumulated merit reached the rank of marquis, while Decheng remained only a valiant-cavalry houseman.
translations.idiomatic: Both elder brothers had risen through merit to marquis, while Decheng remained only a valiant-cavalry houseman.

sentences.zh: 太祖以寧妃故，欲貴顯之。

translations.literal: Because of Consort Ning, the Taizu wished to honor and elevate him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Consort Ning, Taizu wished to honor and elevate him.

sentences.zh: 德成辭。

translations.literal: Decheng declined.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Decheng declined.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 頓首謝曰：「臣性耽曲糵，庸暗不能事事。

translations.literal: He bowed his head and apologized, saying, "By nature your servant is addicted to wine and brew; dull and dim, I cannot manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and said, "Your servant is by nature addicted to drink; dull and incompetent, I cannot manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 位高祿重，必任職司，事不治，上殆殺我。

translations.literal: If my rank were high and my emolument heavy, I would necessarily hold office; if affairs were not well governed, Your Majesty would likely kill me.
translations.idiomatic: With high rank and heavy stipend I would have to hold office; if I failed in my duties, Your Majesty would likely have me executed.

sentences.zh: 人生貴適意，但多得錢、飲醇酒足矣，余非所望。

translations.literal: In life what is precious is contentment; it is enough to have plenty of money and drink good wine; the rest is not what I desire.
translations.idiomatic: What matters in life is contentment; enough money and good wine are all I want—nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善，賜酒百罌，金幣稱之，寵遇益厚。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him, bestowed a hundred jars of wine and gold and silks to match, and favored him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, gave him a hundred jars of wine and matching gold and silks, and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴後苑醉，匍匐脫冠謝。

translations.literal: Once, attending a banquet in the rear garden, he became drunk, crawled on his knees, and removed his cap to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after drinking at a banquet in the rear garden, he crawled forward on his knees and removed his cap to apologize.

sentences.zh: 帝顧見德成發種種，笑曰：「醉風漢，發如此，非酒過耶？

translations.literal: The emperor looked and saw Decheng's hair in disarray and laughed, saying, "Drunken fellow, your hair is like this—is it not the wine's fault?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw Decheng's hair in disarray and laughed, "Drunken fellow—your hair is like this. Isn't that the wine's doing?"

sentences.zh: 」德成仰首曰：「臣猶厭之，盡薙始快。

translations.literal: Decheng raised his head and said, "Your servant still dislikes it; shaving it all off would be a relief."
translations.idiomatic: Decheng looked up and said, "I still dislike it; shaving it all off would be a relief."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 既醒，大懼。

translations.literal: When he sobered up, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When he sobered, he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 佯狂自放，剃髮、衣僧衣，唱佛不已。

translations.literal: He feigned madness and let himself go, shaved his head, wore monk's robes, and chanted Buddhist scriptures without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned madness, shaved his head, put on monk's robes, and chanted Buddhist scriptures without cease.

sentences.zh: 帝謂寧妃曰：「始以汝兄戲言，今實為之，真風漢也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Consort Ning, "At first I took your brother's words as jest; now he has truly done it—a real drunken fellow."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Consort Ning, "At first I took your brother's words as jest; now he has truly done it—the real drunken fellow."

sentences.zh: 」後黨事起，坐死者相屬，德成竟得免。

translations.literal: Later, when the faction affair arose and those sentenced to death followed one after another, Decheng ultimately escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the faction prosecutions came and men were executed in succession, Guo Decheng alone escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 陳德，字至善，濠人。

translations.literal: Chen De, styled Zhishan, was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen De, whose courtesy name was Zhishan, came from Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 世農家，有勇力。

translations.literal: His family had been farmers for generations; he had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations; he was strong and brave.

sentences.zh: 從太祖於定遠，以萬夫長從戰，皆有功，為帳前都先鋒。

translations.literal: He followed the Taizu at Dingyuan; as commander of ten thousand he followed in battle and had merit in each; he became vanguard commander before the tent.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Taizu at Dingyuan; as commander of ten thousand he fought in every engagement with distinction and became vanguard commander in the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 同諸將取寧、徽、衢、婺諸城，擢元帥。

translations.literal: Together with the various generals he took the cities of Ning, Hui, Qu, and Wu, and was promoted to marshal.
translations.idiomatic: With the other generals he took Ningguo, Huizhou, Quzhou, and Wuzhou and was promoted to marshal.

sentences.zh: 李伯升寇長興，德往援，擊走之。

translations.literal: Li Bosheng raided Changxing; De went to relieve it and struck him down in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bosheng raided Changxing, Chen De went to relieve the city and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 從援南昌，大戰鄱陽湖，擒水寨姚平章。

translations.literal: He followed in relieving Nanchang, fought a great battle on Poyang Lake, and captured the water-stockade Pacification Commissioner Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the relief of Nanchang, fought a great battle on Poyang Lake, and captured the water-stockade Pacification Commissioner Yao.

sentences.zh: 太祖舟膠淺，德力戰，身被九矢，不退。

translations.literal: The Taizu's boat ran aground in shallow water; De fought with all his strength, his body struck by nine arrows, and did not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu's boat ran aground in the shallows, Chen De fought with all his strength, took nine arrows in his body, and did not retreat.

sentences.zh: 從平武昌。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 大敗張士誠兵於舊館，擢天策衛親軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He inflicted a great defeat on Zhang Shicheng's troops at Jiuguan and was advanced to commander of the personal guard of the Tiance Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Zhang Shicheng's army at Jiuguan and was promoted to commander of the personal guard of the Tiance Guard.

sentences.zh: 吳平，進僉大都督府事。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was advanced to commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, he was promoted to commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍北取中原，克元汴梁。

translations.literal: He followed the grand general north to take the Central Plain and captured the Yuan capital at Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the grand general north to conquer the Central Plain and captured the Yuan capital at Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 立河南行都督府，以德署府事，討平群盜。

translations.literal: The Henan Branch Chief Military Commission was established; De was appointed to manage its affairs and campaigned to pacify the bandit groups.
translations.idiomatic: When the Henan Branch Chief Military Commission was established, Chen De was put in charge and campaigned to pacify the bandit groups.

sentences.zh: 征山西，破澤州磨盤寨，獲參政喻仁，遂會大軍克平陽、太原、大同。

translations.literal: Campaigning in Shanxi, he broke the Mopan Stockade at Zezhou and captured Administrative Commissioner Yu Ren, then joined the main army in taking Pingyang, Taiyuan, and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shanxi campaign he stormed the Mopan Stockade at Zezhou, captured Administrative Commissioner Yu Ren, and joined the main army in taking Pingyang, Taiyuan, and Datong.

sentences.zh: 渡河取奉元、鳳翔，至秦州，元守將呂國公遁，追擒之。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he took Fengyuan and Fengxiang, reached Qinzhou; the Yuan defender, the Duke of Lü, fled; he pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river to take Fengyuan and Fengxiang, reached Qinzhou; the Yuan defender, the Duke of Lü, fled, and Chen De pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 徐達圍張良臣於慶陽，良臣恃其兄思道為外援，間使往來，德悉擒獲，慶陽遂下。

translations.literal: Xu Da besieged Zhang Liangchen at Qingyang; Liangchen relied on his elder brother Sidao as external support, and messengers went back and forth between them; De captured them all, and Qingyang was thereupon taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da besieged Zhang Liangchen at Qingyang, Liangchen relied on his brother Sidao for outside support; Chen De intercepted every messenger between them, and Qingyang fell.

sentences.zh: 又大破擴廓於古城，降其卒八萬。

translations.literal: Again he inflicted a great defeat on Köke Temür at Gucheng and received the surrender of eighty thousand of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed Köke Temür at Gucheng and accepted the surrender of eighty thousand of his troops.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，封臨江侯，食祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linjiang with an emolument of fifteen hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linjiang with fifteen hundred piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年，從潁川侯傅友德伐蜀，分道入綿州，破龍德，大敗吳友仁之眾，乘勝拔漢州。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the Marquis of Yingchuan, Fu Youde, in campaigning against Shu; entering by separate routes into Mianzhou, he broke Longde and inflicted a great defeat on the forces of Wu Youren, then pressed the advantage to take Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he seconded the Marquis of Yingchuan, Fu Youde, against Shu; entering Mianzhou by a separate route, he stormed Longde, routed Wu Youren's army, and pressed on to take Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 向大亨、戴壽等走成都，追敗之，遂與友德圍成都。

translations.literal: Xiang Daheng, Dai Shou, and others fled to Chengdu; he pursued and defeated them, then together with Youde besieged Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Daheng, Dai Shou, and others fled to Chengdu; he pursued and defeated them, then joined Fu Youde in besieging the city.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，賜白金彩幣。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was bestowed white gold and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, he received gifts of white gold and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 復還汴。

translations.literal: He returned again to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 五年為左副將軍，與馮勝征漠北，破敵於別篤山，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as left deputy general and, with Feng Sheng, campaigned in the northern desert; he defeated the enemy at Biedushan and beheaded and captured by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as left deputy general and, with Feng Sheng, campaigned beyond the northern frontier; at Biedushan he defeated the enemy and took tens of thousands of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 克甘肅，取亦集乃路，留兵扼關而還。

translations.literal: He captured Gansu and took the Yijinai Route, left troops to hold the passes, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Gansu, took the Yijinai Route, left troops to hold the passes, and returned.

sentences.zh: 明年復總兵出朔方，敗敵三岔山，擒其副樞失剌罕等七十余人。

translations.literal: The next year he again commanded the army out of Shuofang, defeated the enemy at Sancha Mountain, and captured Vice Director Shilahang and more than seventy others.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again led the army out of Shuofang, defeated the enemy at Sancha Mountain, and captured Vice Director Shilahang and more than seventy others.

sentences.zh: 其秋，再出戰於答剌海口，斬首六百級，獲其同僉忻都等五十四人。

translations.literal: That autumn he fought again at Dalahaikou, beheaded six hundred, and captured their Associate Commissioner Xindu and fifty-four others.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he fought again at Dalahaikou, took six hundred heads, and captured Associate Commissioner Xindu and fifty-four others.

sentences.zh: 凡三戰三捷。

translations.literal: In all, three battles and three victories.
translations.idiomatic: In three engagements he won three victories.

sentences.zh: 七年練兵北平。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he trained troops in Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he drilled troops in Beiping.

sentences.zh: 十年還鳳陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he returned to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he returned to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 追封杞國公，諡定襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with the posthumous title Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with the temple name Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 子鏞襲封。

translations.literal: His son Yong succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 十六年為征南左副將軍，討平龍泉諸山寇。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he served as left deputy general of the southern expedition and campaigned to pacify the bandits of the Longquan mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he served as left deputy general of the southern expedition and suppressed the bandits of the Longquan mountains.

sentences.zh: 練兵汴梁。

translations.literal: He trained troops at Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled troops at Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 十九年與靖海侯吳禎城會州。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he joined the Marquis of Jinghai, Wu Zhen, at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he joined the Marquis of Jinghai, Wu Zhen, at Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年從馮勝征納哈出，將至金山，與大軍異道相失，敗沒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed Feng Sheng in campaigning against Nahaqu; when they were about to reach Jinshan they lost contact with the main army on a different route and were defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he followed Feng Sheng against Nahaqu; nearing Jinshan on a different route from the main army, his force was cut off and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，追坐德胡惟庸黨，詔書言其征西時有過，被鐫責，遂與惟庸通謀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, in a retrospective prosecution of De as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, the imperial edict stated that on the western campaign he had faults and had been reprimanded and branded, and thereupon conspired with Weiyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, when Chen De was prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, the edict stated that on the western campaign he had been at fault, reprimanded, and branded, and had then conspired with Hu Weiyong.

sentences.zh: 爵除。

translations.literal: The nobility was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 王志，臨淮人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was a man of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi came from Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 以鄉兵從太祖於濠，下滁、和。

translations.literal: As a village soldier he followed the Taizu at Hao and took Chuzhou and Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a village soldier he followed Taizu at Haozhou and helped take Chuzhou and Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，屢騰柵先登，身冒矢石。

translations.literal: Following the crossing of the Yangzi, he repeatedly scaled the palisades first in the assault and exposed himself to arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yangzi crossing he repeatedly scaled the palisades first in the assault and exposed himself to arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 授右副元帥。

translations.literal: He was appointed right vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 從取常州、寧國、江陰。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Changzhou, Ningguo, and Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Changzhou, Ningguo, and Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 復宜興，攻高郵，搗九江，下黃梅，鏖戰鄱陽。

translations.literal: He recovered Yixing, attacked Gaoyou, struck at Jiujiang, took Huangmei, and fought fiercely at Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Yixing, attacked Gaoyou, raided Jiujiang, captured Huangmei, and fought a fierce battle at Lake Poyang.

sentences.zh: 從平武昌，還克廬州，敗張士誠兵，追奔四十里。

translations.literal: Following in the pacification of Wuchang, he returned to take Luzhou, defeated Zhang Shicheng's troops, and pursued the fugitives forty li.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Wuchang, then returned to capture Luzhou, defeated Zhang Shicheng's army, and pursued the fleeing enemy forty li.

sentences.zh: 以親軍衛指揮使改六安衛，守六安。

translations.literal: As commander of the Imperial Bodyguard he was transferred to the Lu'an Guard and garrisoned Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: As commander of the Imperial Bodyguard he was reassigned to the Lu'an Guard to garrison Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 從幸汴梁，渡河，取懷慶、澤、潞，留守平陽。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial tour to Bianliang, crossed the river, took Huaqing, Ze, and Lu, and remained to hold Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Bianliang, crossed the Yellow River, captured Huaqing, Ze, and Lu, and was left behind to hold Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍徐達西伐，會師克興元。

translations.literal: When the grand general Xu Da campaigned westward, their armies joined and took Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Xu Da marched west, their forces united and captured Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，進同知都督府事，封六安侯，歲祿九百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was advanced to vice director of the Chief Military Commission, enfeoffed as Marquis of Lu'an with an annual stipend of nine hundred piculs, and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was promoted to vice director of the Chief Military Commission, enfeoffed as Marquis of Lu'an with an annual stipend of nine hundred piculs of grain, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 移守漢中，帥兵出察罕腦兒塞，還鎮平陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Hanzhong, led troops out through the Chaghan Nayir pass, and returned to command Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to garrison Hanzhong, led troops through the Chaghan Nayir pass, and then returned to command at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 復從大將軍征沙漠。

translations.literal: Again he followed the grand general in campaigning against the desert.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the grand general on campaign into the desert.

sentences.zh: 其後用兵西南，皆以偏將軍從，雖無首功，然持重，未嘗敗衄。

translations.literal: Thereafter, in the southwestern campaigns he always followed as a lieutenant general; though he won no supreme merit, he was steady and never suffered a setback.
translations.idiomatic: In later campaigns in the southwest he always served as a lieutenant general; though he never won the top credit, he was cautious and never suffered a defeat.

sentences.zh: 其攻合肥，敗樓兒張，擒吳副使，為戰功第一。

translations.literal: In the attack on Hefei he defeated Lou'er Zhang, captured a Wu vice commissioner, and ranked first in battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Hefei he defeated Lou'er Zhang, captured a Wu vice commissioner, and was ranked first in battle merit.

sentences.zh: 領山西都司衛所軍務，帝稱其處置得宜。

translations.literal: He took charge of military affairs of the guards and battalions of the Shanxi regional command, and the emperor praised his arrangements as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He took charge of the guards and battalions under the Shanxi regional command, and the emperor praised his handling of affairs.

sentences.zh: 十六年督兵往雲南品甸。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he supervised troops sent to Pindian in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he supervised troops sent to Pindian in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 繕城池，立屯堡，置驛傳，安輯其民。

translations.literal: He repaired city walls, established garrison forts, set up relay stations, and settled and reassured the people.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the city walls, established garrison forts and relay stations, and pacified and settled the local population.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year.

sentences.zh: 追封許國公，諡襄簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Xu, with the posthumous title Xiangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xu with the posthumous title Xiangjian.

sentences.zh: 子威，二十二年嗣侯。

translations.literal: His son Wei in the twenty-second year succeeded to the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei succeeded to the marquisate in the twenty-second year.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐事謫安南衛指揮使。

translations.literal: The next year, for an offense he was demoted to commandant of the Annan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was demoted to commandant of the Annan Guard for an offense.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 弟琙嗣，改清平衛，世襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Juan succeeded, was transferred to the Qingping Guard, and the title was inherited in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Juan succeeded, was reassigned to the Qingping Guard, and the line continued by hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 志亦追坐胡惟庸黨，以死不問。

translations.literal: Zhi was also prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, but because he was already dead no further punishment was applied.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was also prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, but because he was already dead no further punishment was imposed.

sentences.zh: 梅思祖

translations.literal: Mei Sizu
translations.idiomatic: Mei Sizu

sentences.zh: 梅思祖，夏邑人。

translations.literal: Mei Sizu was a man of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Sizu came from Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 初為元義兵元帥，叛從劉福通。

translations.literal: At first he was a Yuan righteous-army marshal, then rebelled and followed Liu Futong.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a marshal in the Yuan loyalist militia, then rebelled and joined Liu Futong.

sentences.zh: 擴廓醢其父。

translations.literal: Köke Temür had his father executed by mincing.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür had his father executed and his body reduced to mincemeat.

sentences.zh: 尋棄福通，歸張士誠，為中書左丞，守淮安。

translations.literal: Soon he abandoned Futong, submitted to Zhang Shicheng, became left vice director of the Secretariat, and garrisoned Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He soon abandoned Liu Futong, went over to Zhang Shicheng, was made left vice director of the Secretariat, and garrisoned Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 徐達兵至，迎降，並獻四州。

translations.literal: When Xu Da's army arrived, he welcomed them in surrender and presented four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da's army arrived, he surrendered and presented four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 士誠殺其兄弟數人。

translations.literal: Shicheng killed several of his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng had several of his brothers killed.

sentences.zh: 太祖擢思祖大都督府副使。

translations.literal: The Taizu promoted Sizu to deputy commissioner of the Metropolitan Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu promoted Mei Sizu to deputy commissioner of the Metropolitan Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 從大軍伐吳，克升山水寨。

translations.literal: Following the main army in the campaign against Wu, he captured the Shenshan water stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main army against Wu and captured the Shenshan water stockade.

sentences.zh: 下湖州，圍平江，皆有功。

translations.literal: He took Huzhou and besieged Pingjiang, in all cases with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Huzhou and took part in the siege of Pingjiang, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 吳平，遷浙江行省右丞。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was transferred to right vice director of the Zhejiang provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, he was appointed right vice director of the Zhejiang provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍伐中原，克山東，取汴、洛，破陝州，下潼關。

translations.literal: Following the grand general in the campaign against the Central Plains, he took Shandong, captured Bian and Luoyang, broke through Shanzhou, and descended on Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the grand general against the Central Plains, conquered Shandong, took Bianliang and Luoyang, stormed Shanzhou, and seized Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 旋師徇河北，至衛輝。

translations.literal: The army wheeled about and swept through Hebei as far as Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: The army then turned north and swept through Hebei as far as Weihui.

sentences.zh: 元平章龍二棄城走彰德，師從之。

translations.literal: The Yuan vice director Long Er abandoned the city and fled to Zhangde; the army followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan vice director Long Er abandoned the city and fled to Zhangde, and the army pursued him.

sentences.zh: 龍二復出走，遂降其城，守之。

translations.literal: Long Er again fled; the city was thereupon reduced and he was left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Long Er fled again; the city was then taken and Mei Sizu was left to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 略定北平未下州郡。

translations.literal: He pacified the prefectures and districts of Beiping not yet subdued.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the remaining prefectures and districts of Beiping under control.

sentences.zh: 從大軍平晉、冀，復從平陝西。

translations.literal: Following the main army he pacified Shanxi and Hebei, and again followed in the pacification of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main army in pacifying Shanxi and Hebei, and again took part in the pacification of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 別將克邠州，獲元參政毛貴等三十人。

translations.literal: As a separate commander he took Binzhou and captured the Yuan vice director Mao Gui and thirty others.
translations.idiomatic: Detached as a separate commander, he captured Binzhou and took the Yuan vice director Mao Gui and thirty others prisoner.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍破擴廓於定西。

translations.literal: Following the grand general he defeated Köke Temür at Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the grand general and defeated Köke Temür at Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 還自秦州，破略陽，入沔州，取興元。

translations.literal: Returning from Qinzhou, he broke through Lueyang, entered Minzhou, and took Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching back from Qinzhou, he stormed Lueyang, entered Minzhou, and captured Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，論功封汝南侯，食祿九百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan with a stipend of nine hundred piculs and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan for his merit, with a stipend of nine hundred piculs of grain and a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 四年伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he campaigned against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took part in the campaign against Shu.

sentences.zh: 五年征甘肅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he campaigned in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he campaigned in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 還命巡視山、陝、遼東城池。

translations.literal: On his return he was ordered to inspect the city defenses of Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was ordered to inspect the fortifications of Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 十四年，四川水盡源、通塔平、散毛諸洞長官作亂，命思祖為征南副將雲南軍，與江夏侯周德興帥兵討平之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the native officials of the cave districts of Shuijinyuan, Tongtaping, and Sanmao in Sichuan rebelled; Sizu was appointed southern expedition deputy general of the Yunnan army, and with the Marquis of Jiangxia, Zhou Dexing, led troops to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the native chiefs of the Shuijinyuan, Tongtaping, and Sanmao cave districts in Sichuan rebelled; Mei Sizu was appointed deputy general of the southern expedition in Yunnan and, with the Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing, led troops to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 十五年復與傅友德平雲南，置貴州都司，以思祖署都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he again joined Fu Youde in pacifying Yunnan; the Guizhou regional command was established, and Sizu was appointed acting regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he again joined Fu Youde in pacifying Yunnan; the Guizhou regional command was established and Mei Sizu was appointed acting regional commander.

sentences.zh: 尋署雲南布政司事，與平章潘元明同守雲南。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed to handle the affairs of the Yunnan provincial administration commission, and together with Vice Director Pan Yuanming he garrisoned Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the Yunnan provincial administration commission and, together with Vice Director Pan Yuanming, garrisoned Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 思祖善撫輯，遠人安之。

translations.literal: Sizu was skilled at pacification and settlement, and the distant peoples were put at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Sizu was skilled at winning people over, and the frontier peoples were reassured.

sentences.zh: 是年卒，賜葬鐘山之陰。

translations.literal: In that year he died and was granted burial on the northern slope of Bell Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year and was granted burial on the northern slope of Bell Mountain.

sentences.zh: 子義，遼東都指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Yi was regional commander of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi served as regional commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十三年追坐思祖胡惟庸黨，滅其家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Sizu was prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, and his entire family was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Mei Sizu was prosecuted retroactively as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, and his entire family was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 思祖從子殷，為駙馬都尉，別有傳。

translations.literal: Sizu's nephew by a collateral line, Yin, served as Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Sizu's collateral nephew Yin served as Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 金朝興

translations.literal: Jin Chaoxing
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chaoxing

sentences.zh: 金朝興，巢人。

translations.literal: Jin Chaoxing was a man of Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chaoxing came from Chao.

sentences.zh: 淮西亂，聚眾結寨自保。

translations.literal: When Huai West was in turmoil he gathered a crowd and fortified a stockade for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: When western Huai was in turmoil he gathered followers and fortified a stockade for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 俞通海等既歸太祖，朝興亦帥眾來附。

translations.literal: After Yu Tonghai and others had submitted to the Taizu, Chaoxing also led his crowd to come over.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Tonghai and others had joined Taizu, Jin Chaoxing also brought his followers to submit.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，征伐皆預，有功。

translations.literal: Following the crossing of the Yangzi, he took part in every campaign and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yangzi crossing he took part in every campaign and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 克常州，為都先鋒。

translations.literal: When Changzhou was taken, he became chief vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Changzhou he was made chief vanguard.

sentences.zh: 復宜興，為左翼副元帥。

translations.literal: When Yixing was recovered, he became left-wing vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the recovery of Yixing he was made left-wing vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 平武昌，進龍驤衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: When Wuchang was pacified, he was advanced to vice commander of the Dragon Pannier Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang was pacified he was promoted to vice commander of the Dragon Pannier Guard.

sentences.zh: 平吳，改鎮武衛指揮使。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was changed to commander of the Suppressing Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified he was appointed commander of the Suppressing Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 克大同，改大同衛指揮使。

translations.literal: When Datong was taken, he was changed to commander of the Datong Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Datong he was reassigned as commander of the Datong Guard.

sentences.zh: 取東勝州，獲元平章劉麟等十八人。

translations.literal: He took Dongsheng Prefecture and captured the Yuan vice director Liu Lin and eighteen others.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Dongsheng Prefecture and took the Yuan vice director Liu Lin and eighteen others prisoner.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，論功為都督僉事兼秦王左相。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, for merit he became commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and concurrently left counselor to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was made commissioner of the Chief Military Commission and concurrently left counselor to the Prince of Qin for his merit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，解都督府事，專傅王。

translations.literal: Before long he was relieved of metropolitan military commission duties and devoted himself exclusively to tutoring the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was relieved of his duties at the metropolitan military commission and devoted himself exclusively to tutoring the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 四年從大軍伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the main army in the campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed the main army against Shu.

sentences.zh: 七年帥師至黑城，獲元太尉盧伯顏、平章帖兒不花並省院等官二十五人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he led troops to Heicheng and captured the Yuan grand defender Lu Boyan, the vice director Tie'erbuluhua, and twenty-five officials of the secretariat and ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he led troops to Heicheng and captured the Yuan grand defender Lu Boyan, Vice Director Tie'erbuluhua, and twenty-five officials of the secretariat and ministries.

sentences.zh: 遂從李文忠分領東道兵，取和林，語具文忠傳。

translations.literal: He then followed Li Wenzhong in jointly leading the eastern-route army to take Karakorum; the details are given in Wenzhong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Li Wenzhong in jointly commanding the eastern-route army to take Karakorum; the full account is given in Li Wenzhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 朝興沉勇有智略，所至以偏師取勝，雖未為大帥，而功出諸將上。

translations.literal: Chaoxing was deep, brave, and resourceful; wherever he went he won with detached columns, and though he never served as supreme commander, his achievements ranked above those of the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chaoxing was resolute, brave, and resourceful; wherever he went he won victories with detached columns, and though he never held supreme command, his achievements surpassed those of the other generals.

sentences.zh: 十一年從沐英西征，收納鄰七站地。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed Mu Ying on the western expedition and recovered the territory of the seven Naolin stations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he followed Mu Ying on the western expedition and recovered the territory of the seven Naolin stations.

sentences.zh: 明年論功封宣德侯，祿二千石，世襲指揮使。

translations.literal: The next year, for merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuande with a stipend of two thousand piculs and hereditary commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuande for his merit, with a stipend of two thousand piculs of grain and hereditary rank as commandant.

sentences.zh: 十五年從傅友德征雲南，駐師臨安，元右丞兀卜台、元帥完者都、土酋楊政等俱降。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Fu Youde in the campaign against Yunnan and encamped at Lin'an; the Yuan right vice director Wubutai, the marshal Wanzhedu, and the tribal chief Yang Zheng all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he followed Fu Youde against Yunnan and encamped at Lin'an; the Yuan right vice director Wubutai, Marshal Wanzhedu, and the tribal chief Yang Zheng all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 朝興撫輯有方，軍民咸悅。

translations.literal: Chaoxing was skilled in pacification; soldiers and civilians alike were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chaoxing was skilled at winning people over, and both soldiers and civilians were pleased with his rule.

sentences.zh: 進次會川卒，追封沂國公，諡武毅。

translations.literal: Advancing he halted at Huichuan and died; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Yi, with the posthumous title Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Huichuan and died there; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yi with the posthumous title Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 十七年論平雲南功，改錫世侯券，增祿五百石。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, in recognition of merit in pacifying Yunnan, his hereditary marquis certificate was reissued and his stipend increased by five hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, in recognition of his merit in pacifying Yunnan, he was granted a new hereditary marquis patent and his stipend was increased by five hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 唐勝宗

translations.literal: Tang Shengzong
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shengzong

sentences.zh: 唐勝宗，濠人。

translations.literal: Tang Shengzong was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shengzong came from Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵，勝宗年十八，來歸。

translations.literal: When the Taizu raised his army, Shengzong was eighteen and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu raised his army, Tang Shengzong was eighteen and came to join him.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，積功為中翼元帥。

translations.literal: Following the crossing of the Yangzi, through accumulated merit he became marshal of the central wing.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yangzi crossing he rose through accumulated merit to become marshal of the central wing.

sentences.zh: 從徐達克常州，進圍寧國，扼險力戰，敗其援兵。

translations.literal: Following Xu Da in the taking of Changzhou, he advanced to besiege Ningguo, held the strategic passes, fought fiercely, and defeated the relief army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in capturing Changzhou, then advanced to besiege Ningguo, held the strategic passes, fought fiercely, and defeated the relief army.

sentences.zh: 城遂降。

translations.literal: The city thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The city then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從征婺州，克之。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Wuzhou, he took it.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Wuzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 從征池州，力戰，敗陳友諒兵，擢龍驤衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Chizhou, he fought fiercely, defeated Chen Youliang's troops, and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Dragon Pannier Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the campaign against Chizhou he fought fiercely, defeated Chen Youliang's army, and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Dragon Pannier Guard.

sentences.zh: 從征友諒，至安慶，敵固守。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Youliang, when they reached Anqing the enemy held firm.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Chen Youliang, when the army reached Anqing the enemy held firm.

sentences.zh: 勝宗為陸兵疑之，出不意，搗克其水寨。

translations.literal: Shengzong led land troops to feign against them; taking them unawares, he stormed and captured their water stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shengzong led land troops in a diversionary attack; catching the enemy off guard, he stormed and captured their water stockade.

sentences.zh: 從下南昌，略定江西諸郡。
