translations.literal: Following in the taking of Nanchang, he pacified the prefectures of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Nanchang and pacified the prefectures of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 援安豐，攻廬州，戰鄱陽，邀擊涇江口，皆有功。

translations.literal: He relieved Anfeng, attacked Luzhou, fought at Poyang, and intercepted at the mouth of the Jing River, in all cases with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Anfeng, attacked Luzhou, fought at Lake Poyang, and intercepted the enemy at the mouth of the Jing River, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 擢驃騎衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commander of the Flying Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander of the Flying Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 從定武昌，徇長沙、沅陵、澧陽。

translations.literal: Following in the pacification of Wuchang, he swept through Changsha, Yuanling, and Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Wuchang and swept through Changsha, Yuanling, and Liyang.

sentences.zh: 從徐達取江陵，還定淮東。

translations.literal: Following Xu Da in the taking of Jiangling, he returned to pacify eastern Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in capturing Jiangling, then returned to pacify eastern Huai.

sentences.zh: 穴城克安豐，追獲元將忻都。

translations.literal: By tunneling under the city he took Anfeng and pursued and captured the Yuan general Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He tunneled under the walls to capture Anfeng and pursued and captured the Yuan general Xindu.

sentences.zh: 為安豐衛指揮使守之。

translations.literal: He became commander of the Anfeng Guard and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of the Anfeng Guard and garrisoned the city.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍伐中原，克汴梁、歸德、許州，輒留守。

translations.literal: Following the grand general in the campaign against the Central Plains, he took Bianliang, Guide, and Xuzhou, and was repeatedly left behind to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the grand general against the Central Plains, captured Bianliang, Guide, and Xuzhou, and was repeatedly left behind to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 從大軍克延安，進都督府同知。

translations.literal: Following the main army in the taking of Yan'an, he was advanced to vice director of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main army in capturing Yan'an and was promoted to vice director of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年冬封延安侯，食祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yan'an with a stipend of fifteen hundred piculs and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yan'an with a stipend of fifteen hundred piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 坐擅馳驛騎，奪爵，降指揮。

translations.literal: For unauthorized use of relay mounts he was deprived of his nobility and demoted to commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For unauthorized use of relay mounts he was stripped of his title and demoted to commandant.

sentences.zh: 捕代縣反者。

translations.literal: He captured the rebels of Dai County.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the rebels in Dai County.

sentences.zh: 久之，復爵。

translations.literal: After a long while his nobility was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 十四年，浙東山寇葉丁香等作亂，命總兵討之，擒賊首並其黨三千余人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the mountain bandits Ye Dingxiang and others rebelled in eastern Zhejiang; he was ordered to command troops to suppress them and captured the ringleaders and more than three thousand of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the mountain bandits Ye Dingxiang and others rebelled in eastern Zhejiang; he was ordered to lead troops against them and captured the ringleaders and more than three thousand of their followers.

sentences.zh: 分兵平安福賊，至臨安，降元右丞兀卜台等。

translations.literal: He divided his forces to pacify the bandits of Ping'anfu, reached Lin'an, and received the surrender of the Yuan right vice director Wubutai and others.
translations.idiomatic: He detached columns to pacify the bandits of Ping'anfu, advanced to Lin'an, and received the surrender of the Yuan right vice director Wubutai and others.

sentences.zh: 十五年巡視陝西，督屯田，簡軍士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he inspected Shaanxi, supervised garrison farming, and streamlined the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu he toured Shaanxi, overseeing military colonies and weeding out unfit soldiers.

sentences.zh: 明年鎮遼東，奉敕勿通高麗。

translations.literal: The next year he was posted to guard Liaodong, with an imperial order not to have dealings with Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took command in Liaodong under orders to keep all contact with Goryeo cut off.

sentences.zh: 高麗使至，察其奸，表聞。

translations.literal: When a Goryeo envoy arrived, he detected their treachery and memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When a Goryeo embassy came, he saw through their designs and reported it to the court.

sentences.zh: 賜敕褒美，比魏田豫卻烏桓賂，稱名臣。

translations.literal: An edict of praise was granted, comparing him to Wei Tianyu of Wei who rejected Wuhuan bribes, and calling him a famed minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a commendatory edict, likening him to Wei Tianyu of Wei, who had spurned Wuhuan bribes, and hailing him as a true statesman.

sentences.zh: 在鎮七年，威信大著。

translations.literal: In seven years at his post his prestige and authority grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years on the frontier his authority was firmly established.

sentences.zh: 召還，帥師討平貴州蠻。

translations.literal: Recalled, he led troops to pacify the Miao rebels of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to lead an expedition that crushed the Guizhou Miao uprising.

sentences.zh: 練兵黃平。

translations.literal: He drilled troops at Huangping.
translations.idiomatic: He trained his army at Huangping.

sentences.zh: 二十三年坐胡惟庸黨誅，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, for membership in Hu Weiyong's faction he was executed and his marquisate abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was put to death as a partisan of Hu Weiyong, and his title was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 陸仲亨

translations.literal: Lu Zhongheng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhongheng

sentences.zh: 陸仲亨，濠人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhongheng was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhongheng came from Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖，從征滁州，取大柳樹諸寨。

translations.literal: He submitted to the Taizu and followed the campaigns, taking Chuzhou and capturing the stockades of Daliushu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Taizu, fought at Chuzhou, and stormed the Daliushu strongholds.

sentences.zh: 克和陽，擊敗元兵。

translations.literal: He took Heyang and defeated Yuan troops.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Heyang and routed the Yuan army.

sentences.zh: 逐青山群盜。

translations.literal: He drove off the bandit hosts of Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: He scattered the Qingshan bandits.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，取太平，定集慶，從徐達下諸郡縣。

translations.literal: He crossed the Yangzi with the army, took Taiping, secured Jiqing, and with Xu Da reduced the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yangzi with the main force, he helped take Taiping and Jiqing and, under Xu Da, swept the lower Yangzi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 授左翼統軍元帥。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Wing Commander-in-Chief Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Wing Commander-in-Chief Marshal.

sentences.zh: 從征陳友諒，功多，進驃騎衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Chen Youliang, he won many merits and was advanced to commander of the Flying Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the war against Chen Youliang his service was distinguished, and he rose to command the Flying Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春討贛州，降熊天瑞，為贛州衛指揮使，節制嶺南北新附諸郡。

translations.literal: With Chang Yuchun he attacked Ganzhou, Xiong Tianrui surrendered, and he became commander of the Ganzhou Guard, controlling the newly submitted prefectures north and south of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chang Yuchun he besieged Ganzhou; when Xiong Tianrui submitted, he was left as commander of the Ganzhou Guard with authority over the newly pacified Lingnan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 調兵克梅州、會昌、湘鄉，悉平諸山寨。

translations.literal: He shifted troops to take Meizhou, Huichang, and Xiangxiang, and all the mountain stockades were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Detaching forces, he seized Meizhou, Huichang, and Xiangxiang and cleared every mountain stronghold.

sentences.zh: 十二年與周德興、黃彬等從湯和練兵臨清。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, with Zhou Dexing, Huang Bin, and others he followed Tang He in drilling troops at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he joined Zhou Dexing, Huang Bin, and the rest under Tang He to train troops at Linqing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，即軍中逮三人至京，既而釋之。

translations.literal: Before long, three men were seized in camp and sent to the capital; afterward they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward three officers were arrested in camp and hauled to the capital, then set free again.

sentences.zh: 移鎮成都，平巨津州叛蠻。

translations.literal: Transferred to garrison Chengdu, he pacified the rebel Miao of Jujin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to Chengdu, he put down the Jujin Prefecture Miao revolt.

sentences.zh: 烏撒諸蠻復叛，從傅友德討平之。

translations.literal: When the Wusa tribes rebelled again, he followed Fu Youde and crushed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wusa tribes rose once more, he marched with Fu Youde and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，治胡惟庸逆黨，家奴封貼木告仲亨與勝宗、費聚、趙庸皆與通謀，下吏訊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, while investigating Hu Weiyong's treasonous faction, the household slave Feng Tiemuh reported that Zhongheng, together with Shengzong, Fei Ju, and Zhao Yong, had all joined in conspiracy, and they were handed to the judicial officers for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, as Hu Weiyong's plot was being prosecuted, Zhongheng's bondservant Feng Tiemuh accused him, along with Tang Shengzong, Fei Ju, and Zhao Yong, of complicity; all were committed for trial.

sentences.zh: 獄具，帝曰：「朕每怪其居貴位有憂色。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, the Emperor said: "I have often wondered at his worried look despite holding a lofty rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was closed, the Emperor said, "I always found it strange that a man of such rank wore so troubled a face.

sentences.zh: 」遂誅仲亨，籍其家。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zhongheng was executed and his household confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: " He was executed, and his property was seized.

sentences.zh: 初，仲亨年十七，為亂兵所掠。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongheng was seventeen, he was seized by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, at seventeen, he had been captured by rampaging soldiers.

sentences.zh: 父母兄弟俱亡，持一升麥伏草間。

translations.literal: Parents, brothers, and kin were all dead; clutching a sheng of wheat he hid in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: His parents and brothers were dead; he crouched in the weeds with only a measure of wheat to his name.

sentences.zh: 帝見之，呼曰「來」，遂從征伐，至封侯。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw him and called, "Come," and thereafter he followed the campaigns until enfeoffment as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu spotted him and called, "Come here!" From that day he fought at the Emperor's side until he won a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「此我初起時腹心股肱也。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "In my earliest rise he was the man at my belly, heart, thigh, and arm.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had once said of him, "In the days when I first raised my banner, he was flesh at my core—belly, heart, thigh, and arm.

sentences.zh: 」竟誅死。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he died by the headsman's blade.

sentences.zh: 費聚，字子英，五河人。

translations.literal: Fei Ju, styled Ziying, was a man of Wuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Ju, whose courtesy name was Ziying, came from Wuhe.

sentences.zh: 父德興，以材勇為游徼卒。

translations.literal: His father Dexing, for talent and courage, served as a patrol militiaman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dexing, a man of strength and daring, had served as a local patrol militiaman.

sentences.zh: 聚少習技擊。

translations.literal: Ju in youth practiced the martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Ju trained in arms from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 太祖遇於濠，偉其貌，深相結納。

translations.literal: The Taizu met him at Hao, admired his stature, and drew him into close friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu met him at Haozhou, was struck by his imposing frame, and took him into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 定遠張家堡有民兵，無所屬，郭子興欲招之，念無可使者。

translations.literal: At Zhangjiabao in Dingyuan there were militia with no allegiance; Guo Zixing wished to recruit them but had no envoy.
translations.idiomatic: A militia force at Zhangjiabao in Dingyuan stood without a master; Guo Zixing wanted them but lacked someone to treat with them.

sentences.zh: 太祖力疾請行，偕聚騎而往，步卒九人俱。

translations.literal: Though still ill, the Taizu pressed to go, riding out with Ju; nine foot soldiers went along as well.
translations.idiomatic: Though still recovering from illness, the Taizu insisted on going himself, riding out with Ju and nine foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 至寶公河，望其營甚整，弓弩皆外向。

translations.literal: Reaching the Baogong River, they saw the camp in good order, bows and crossbows all facing outward.
translations.idiomatic: At the Baogong River they saw a camp in tight order, every bow and crossbow trained outward.

sentences.zh: 步卒懼，欲走。

translations.literal: The foot soldiers were afraid and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry panicked and wanted to run.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「彼以騎蹴我，走將安往？

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "If their horsemen trample us, where can we flee?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said, "If their cavalry rides us down, where will we run?

sentences.zh: 」遂前抵其營。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they advanced straight to the camp.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed on into the camp.

sentences.zh: 招諭已定，約三日。

translations.literal: Persuasion was settled and a three-day tryst agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He won them over in talk and fixed a rendezvous in three days.

sentences.zh: 太祖先歸，留聚俟之。

translations.literal: The Taizu returned first and left Ju to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu rode back first, leaving Ju to keep the appointment.

sentences.zh: 其帥欲他屬，聚還報。

translations.literal: Their commander wished to submit elsewhere; Ju returned and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The militia leader then tried to offer himself to another patron; Ju rode back with word of it.

sentences.zh: 太祖復偕聚以三百人往，計縛其帥，收卒三千人。

translations.literal: The Taizu again went with Ju with three hundred men, planning to bind their commander and take three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu returned with Ju and three hundred men, seized the commander by stratagem, and enrolled three thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 豁鼻山有秦把頭八百余人，聚復招降之。

translations.literal: On Huobi Mountain there were more than eight hundred under Bandit Chief Qin; Ju again induced them to submit.
translations.idiomatic: More than eight hundred followers of Bandit Chief Qin held Huobi Mountain; Ju talked them into surrender as well.

sentences.zh: 遂從取靈璧，克泗、滁、和州。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed in taking Lingbi and capturing Si, Chu, and He prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He then fought at Lingbi and helped take Si, Chu, and He prefectures.

sentences.zh: 授承信校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Credentialed Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Credentialed Commandant.

sentences.zh: 既定江東，克長興，立永興翼元帥府，以聚副耿炳文為元帥。

translations.literal: Once the lower Yangzi was settled, he took Changxing; the Yongxing Wing Marshal's Office was established, with Ju as deputy marshal to Geng Bingwen.
translations.idiomatic: After the southeast was won, he took part in the capture of Changxing; when the Yongxing Wing Marshal's Office was set up, Ju served as deputy to Geng Bingwen.

sentences.zh: 張士誠入寇，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shicheng raided, he defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He repulsed Zhang Shicheng's invasions.

sentences.zh: 召領宿衛。

translations.literal: He was summoned to command the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to lead the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 援安豐，兩定江西，克武昌，皆從。

translations.literal: Relieving Anfeng, twice pacifying Jiangxi, and taking Wuchang—he was present at all.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at the relief of Anfeng, in both Jiangxi campaigns, and at the fall of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 改永興翼元帥府為永興親軍指揮司，仍副炳文為指揮同知。

translations.literal: The Yongxing Wing Marshal's Office was changed to the Yongxing Personal Army Command, and he remained deputy to Bingwen as Associate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongxing Wing was reorganized as the Yongxing Personal Army Command, and he stayed on as Geng Bingwen's second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 士誠復入寇，獲其帥宋興祖，再敗之。

translations.literal: When Shicheng raided again, he captured their commander Song Xingzu and defeated them once more.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng attacked again, he took their general Song Xingzu and beat them back a second time.

sentences.zh: 士誠奪氣，不敢復窺長興。

translations.literal: Shicheng lost heart and dared not again look toward Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng lost his nerve and never again threatened Changxing.

sentences.zh: 隨征淮安、湖州、平江，皆有功，進指揮使。

translations.literal: In the campaigns on Huaian, Huzhou, and Pingjiang he had merit at each and was advanced to commander.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at Huaian, Huzhou, and Pingjiang and was promoted to guard commander.

sentences.zh: 湯和討方國珍，聚以舟師從海道邀擊。

translations.literal: When Tang He attacked Fang Guozhen, Ju with the fleet struck by sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang He's campaign against Fang Guozhen, he led the naval wing along the coast to cut off escape.

sentences.zh: 浙東平，復由海道取福州，破延平。

translations.literal: When eastern Zhe was pacified, he again took Fuzhou by sea and broke Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: After eastern Zhe was secured, he sailed to take Fuzhou and stormed Yanping.

sentences.zh: 歸次昌國，剿海寇葉、陳二姓於蘭秀山。

translations.literal: On the return he halted at Changguo and suppressed sea bandits of the Ye and Chen clans at Lanshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the homeward march he paused at Changguo and wiped out Ye and Chen pirates off Lanshou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至是，聚始獨將。

translations.literal: Only then did Ju first command an army on his own.
translations.idiomatic: It was the first time he had held independent command.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年會大軍取西安，改西安衛指揮使，進都督府僉事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu he joined the main army in taking Xi'an, was made commander of the Xi'an Guard, and advanced to associate commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year two he helped take Xi'an, was appointed commander of the Xi'an Guard, and rose to associate commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 鎮守平涼。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to garrison Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 三年封平涼侯，歲祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingliang with an annual emolument of fifteen hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he received the marquisate of Pingliang, fifteen hundred piculs of grain yearly, and a patent of hereditary entitlement.

sentences.zh: 時諸將在邊屯田募伍，歲有常課。

translations.literal: At that time the generals on the frontier garrisoned fields and recruited soldiers, each with a fixed annual quota.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders then ran military farms and filled their rolls to set annual quotas.

sentences.zh: 聚頗耽酒色，無所事事。

translations.literal: Ju was much given to wine and women and did nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sank into drink and dalliance and neglected his duties.

sentences.zh: 又以招降無功，召還，切責之。

translations.literal: Also, for achieving nothing in inducing surrender, he was recalled and sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: When his pacification efforts came to nothing, he was summoned back and sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 明年從傅友德征雲南，大戰白石江，擒達里麻。

translations.literal: The next year he followed Fu Youde's Yunnan expedition; at the great battle on the Baishi River he captured Dalima.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he marched with Fu Youde into Yunnan and, at the great battle on the Baishi River, took Dalima prisoner.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，進取大理。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified, he pressed on to take Dali.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan fell, he helped seize Dali.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸蠻復叛，命副安陸侯吳復為總兵。

translations.literal: Before long the tribes rebelled again; he was ordered to serve as deputy to Marquis Wu Fu of Anlu as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the tribes rose again; he was made second to Marquis Wu Fu of Anlu as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 授以方略，分攻關索嶺及阿咱等寨，悉下之。

translations.literal: Tactics were entrusted to him; dividing forces he attacked Guansuo Ridge and the stockades of Aza and the rest, and all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Given a free hand in strategy, he split his forces against Guansuo Ridge and the Aza stockades and reduced them all.

sentences.zh: 蠻地始定。

translations.literal: The tribal lands were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal country was finally quieted.

sentences.zh: 置貴州都指揮使司，以聚署司事。

translations.literal: The Guizhou Chief Military Commission was established, with Ju acting as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guizhou Chief Military Commission was founded, Ju was left in charge.

sentences.zh: 十八年命為總兵官，帥指揮丁忠等征廣南，擒火立達，俘其眾萬人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed supreme commander and led Commanders Ding Zhong and others against Guangnan, capturing Huolida and taking ten thousand of his followers prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was named supreme commander, led Ding Zhong and other commanders into Guangnan, seized Huolida, and took ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 還鎮雲南。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to his post in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 二十三年召還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 李善長敗，語連聚。

translations.literal: When Li Shanchang fell, his case implicated Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shanchang's downfall dragged Ju into the net.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「聚曩使姑蘇不稱旨，朕嘗詈責，遂欲反耶！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Ju once served at Gusu and displeased me; I cursed and rebuked him—did he then wish to rebel!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When I sent Ju to pacify Suzhou he failed me; I berated him then—was he plotting revolt all along?

sentences.zh: 」竟坐黨死，爵除。

translations.literal: " In the end he died as a partisan, and his marquisate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " He was executed as a conspirator, and his title was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 子超，征方國珍，沒於陣。

translations.literal: His son Chao, campaigning against Fang Guozhen, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao fell fighting Fang Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 璿，以人材舉官江西參政。

translations.literal: Xuan, recommended for talent, became administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan, nominated for ability, rose to administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 孫宏，從征雲南，積功為右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His grandson Hong, on the Yunnan expedition, accumulated merit and became commander of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Hong earned distinction in Yunnan and became commander of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐奏對不實，戍金齒。

translations.literal: For presenting a false report at court he was banished to garrison Jinchi.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to military service at Jinchi for lying in a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 陸聚，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Lu Ju; his native place is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ju—his origins are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 元樞密院同知。

translations.literal: He was associate commissioner of the Yuan Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He had served the Yuan as associate commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 脫脫敗芝{艹麻}李於徐州，彭大等奔濠。

translations.literal: When Tuo Tuo defeated Zhima Li at Xuzhou, Peng Da and others fled to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuo Tuo routed Zhima Li at Xuzhou, Peng Da and his followers poured into Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 聚撫戢流亡，繕城保境，寇不敢犯。

translations.literal: Ju soothed the displaced, repaired the walls, and guarded the territory, and raiders did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sheltered refugees, rebuilt the walls, and held the border until bandits no longer dared approach.

sentences.zh: 徐達經理江、淮，聚以徐、宿二州降。

translations.literal: When Xu Da organized the Jianghuai region, Ju surrendered Xu and Su prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da moved to secure the Jianghuai, Ju submitted Xu and Su prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗詔諭：「二州，吾桑梓地，未忍加兵。

translations.literal: The Taizu once issued an edict saying: "These two prefectures are the land of my nativity; I could not bear to send troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had once proclaimed, "Those two prefectures are my homeland—I could not bring myself to attack them.

sentences.zh: 」及歸附，大悅。

translations.literal: " When they submitted he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " When they came over to him, his joy was boundless.

sentences.zh: 以聚為江南行省參政，仍守徐州。

translations.literal: Ju was made administrative commissioner of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and continued to guard Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He made Ju administrative commissioner of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat while leaving him to hold Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣兵略定沛、魚台、邳、蕭、宿遷、睢寧。

translations.literal: He sent troops to secure Pei, Yutai, Pi, Xiao, Suqian, and Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sent columns to bring Pei, Yutai, Pi, Xiao, Suqian, and Suining under control.

sentences.zh: 擴廓遣李左丞侵徐，駐陵子村。

translations.literal: Kökö Temür sent Vice Minister Li to invade Xu and encamped at Lingzi Village.
translations.idiomatic: Kökö Temür dispatched Vice Minister Li against Xuzhou, who pitched camp at Lingzi Village.

sentences.zh: 聚遣指揮傅友德擊之，俘其眾，擒李左丞。

translations.literal: Ju sent Commander Fu Youde to attack; he captured the enemy host and took Vice Minister Li prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sent Fu Youde to strike; the Yuan force was shattered and Vice Minister Li was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 又敗元兵於宿州，擒僉院邢端等。

translations.literal: He again defeated Yuan troops at Suzhou and captured Commissioner Xing Duan and others.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the Yuan again at Suzhou and seized Commissioner Xing Duan and his officers.

sentences.zh: 從定山東，平汴梁。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Shandong and taking Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on to pacify Shandong and take Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 還鎮，改山東行省參政。

translations.literal: Returning to his post, he was made administrative commissioner of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Back on the frontier he was promoted to administrative commissioner of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從平元都，略大同、保定、真定。

translations.literal: He followed in taking the Yuan capital and reduced Datong, Baoding, and Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the fall of Dadu and the reduction of Datong, Baoding, and Zhending.

sentences.zh: 攻克車子山及鳳山、城山、鐵山諸寨，分守井陘故關，會師陝西，克承天寨。

translations.literal: He stormed Chezishan and the stockades of Fengshan, Chengshan, and Tieshan, garrisoned the old Jingxing Pass in detachments, joined the Shaanxi army, and took Chengtian Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Chezishan and the Fengshan, Chengshan, and Tieshan strongholds, posted detachments at the old Jingxing Pass, united with the Shaanxi column, and seized Chengtian Stockade.

sentences.zh: 聚所部皆淮北勁卒，雖燕、趙精騎不及也。

translations.literal: Ju's command were all crack troops of north Huai, whom even the fine cavalry of Yan and Zhao could not match.
translations.idiomatic: His men were the hard fighters of north Huai—cavalry from Yan and Zhao were their inferior.

sentences.zh: 北征，沂、邳山民乘間作亂，召聚還，討平之。

translations.literal: On the northern expedition, mountaineers of Yi and Pi rose in disorder; Ju was recalled and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaign, hill people of Yi and Pi rebelled; Ju was called back and put them down.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，封河南侯，歲祿九百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Henan with an annual emolument of nine hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year three he was created Marquis of Henan with nine hundred piculs yearly and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 八年，同衛國公愈屯田陝西，置衛戍守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Duke of Wei Guo Yu he established garrison agriculture in Shaanxi and set up guards to hold the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined Xu Da, Duke of Wei, in opening garrison farms in Shaanxi and establishing guard posts to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十二年同信國公和練兵臨清。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, together with Duke of Xin Guo He he drilled troops at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he joined Tang He, Duke of Xin, in drilling troops at Linqing.

sentences.zh: 尋理福建軍務。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he oversaw Fujian military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of military affairs in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 召還，賜第鳳陽。

translations.literal: Called back to court, he was granted a residence at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was granted a mansion at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 二十三年坐胡惟庸黨死，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was executed as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, and his title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was put to death on charges of belonging to Hu Weiyong's faction, and his marquisate was revoked.

sentences.zh: 鄭遇春

translations.literal: Zheng Yuchun
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuchun

sentences.zh: 鄭遇春，濠人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuchun was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuchun came from Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 與兄遇霖俱以勇力聞。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Yulin were both renowned for courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Yulin were both famed for their courage and physical prowess.

sentences.zh: 遇霖與裡人有郤，欲殺之，遇春力護，得解取。

translations.literal: Yulin had a grudge against a fellow townsman and wanted to kill him; Yuchun vigorously protected the man, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin bore a grudge against a neighbor and meant to kill him; Yuchun shielded the man with all his strength until the quarrel was resolved.

sentences.zh: 眾皆畏遇霖，而以遇春為賢。

translations.literal: Everyone feared Yulin, but regarded Yuchun as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: All feared Yulin, yet looked on Yuchun as the better man.

sentences.zh: 太祖下滁州，遇霖為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Taizu descended on Chuzhou, Yulin served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched on Chuzhou, Yulin led the van.

sentences.zh: 取鐵佛岡、三郤河、大柳等寨，遇春亦累功至總管。

translations.literal: They took the stockades at Tiefo Ridge, Sanxi River, Daliu, and elsewhere; Yuchun too accumulated merit until he reached the rank of commandant-general.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the stockades at Tiefo Ridge, Sanxi River, Daliu, and the like; Yuchun likewise piled up merit until he rose to commandant-general.

sentences.zh: 攻蕪湖，遇霖戰死，遇春領其眾。

translations.literal: In the assault on Wuhu, Yulin died in battle, and Yuchun took command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the attack on Wuhu, Yulin fell in battle, and Yuchun assumed command of his force.

sentences.zh: 時諸將所部不過千人，遇春兼兩隊，而所部尤驍果。

translations.literal: At the time no general commanded more than a thousand men; Yuchun held two companies together, and his troops were especially fierce and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: In those days no commander led more than a thousand men; Yuchun held two companies under his hand, and his men were the boldest and hardest-hitting of all.

sentences.zh: 累戰功多，授左翼元帥。

translations.literal: After many battles and much merit, he was appointed Left-wing Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: With battle upon battle and merit heaped upon merit, he was made Left-wing Marshal.

sentences.zh: 從平陳友諒，身先士卒，未嘗自言功，太祖異之。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign to pacify Chen Youliang, always leading from the front, and never claimed credit for himself—Taizu marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Chen Youliang, always charging ahead of his men and never once boasting of his deeds—Taizu marked him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 取六安，為六安衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He took Lu'an and was made assistant commander of the Lu'an Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Lu'an he was appointed assistant commander of the Lu'an Guard.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍定山東、河南北，克朔州，改朔州衛指揮副使。

translations.literal: He followed the grand general in pacifying Shandong and the lands north of the Yellow River, captured Shuozhou, and was reassigned as deputy commander of the Shuozhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the grand general in pacifying Shandong and the country north of the Yellow River, took Shuozhou, and was transferred to deputy commander of the Shuozhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，進同知大都督府事，封滎陽侯，歲祿九百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was promoted to vice director of the Chief Military Commission, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang with an annual stipend of nine hundred piculs, and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was advanced to vice director of the Chief Military Commission, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang with an annual stipend of nine hundred piculs of grain, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 明年命駐臨濠，開行大都督府。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered to garrison at Linhao and establish a traveling Chief Military Commission there.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was ordered to garrison Linhao and open a traveling Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 坐累奪爵。

translations.literal: For accumulated offenses his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated offenses he was stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 尋復之，復守朔州。

translations.literal: Before long it was restored, and he again held Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the title was restored, and he returned to hold Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 從傅友德平雲南，帥楊文等經略城池屯堡。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Youde in pacifying Yunnan and directed Yang Wen and others in organizing walled cities and garrison forts.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Youde in the pacification of Yunnan and, with Yang Wen and others, laid out walled cities and garrison forts.

sentences.zh: 還京，督金吾諸衛，造海船百八十艘，運餉遼東，籍陝西岷州諸衛官馬。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he oversaw the Golden Guard and other guards, built one hundred eighty seagoing vessels, shipped provisions to Liaodong, and registered government horses of the Minzhou and other guards in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the capital he supervised the Golden Guard and other guards, built one hundred eighty seagoing ships, transported provisions to Liaodong, and registered the government horses of Minzhou and the other guards in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十三年坐胡惟庸黨死。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was executed as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was put to death as a member of Hu Weiyong's faction.

sentences.zh: 爵除。

translations.literal: His title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His marquisate was revoked.

sentences.zh: 黃彬，江夏人。

translations.literal: Huang Bin was a man of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Bin came from Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 從歐普祥攻陷袁、吉屬縣，徐壽輝以普祥守袁州。

translations.literal: Following Ou Puxiang, he stormed the counties subordinate to Yuanzhou and Jizhou; Xu Shouhui appointed Puxiang to hold Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ou Puxiang in overrunning the counties under Yuanzhou and Jizhou; Xu Shouhui then left Puxiang to hold Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及陳友諒殺壽輝，僭偽號，彬言於普祥曰：「公與友諒比肩，奈何下之？

translations.literal: When Chen Youliang murdered Shouhui and usurped a royal title, Bin said to Puxiang: "You and Youliang stand as equals—why submit to him?
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang killed Shouhui and set himself up with a royal title, Bin said to Puxiang, "You and Youliang are peers—why bow beneath him?

sentences.zh: 友諒驕恣，非江東敵也。

translations.literal: Youliang is arrogant and overbearing; he is no match for the armies east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang is proud and reckless; he cannot stand against the armies east of the river.

sentences.zh: 保境候東師，當不失富貴。

translations.literal: Hold your territory and await the eastern armies, and you should not lose wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Hold your ground and wait for the eastern host, and you will keep your wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 」普祥遂遣使納款。

translations.literal: Puxiang then sent envoys to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: Puxiang thereupon sent envoys to declare his submission.

sentences.zh: 友諒遣弟友仁攻之。

translations.literal: Youliang sent his younger brother Youren to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang dispatched his younger brother Youren to attack him.

sentences.zh: 彬與普祥敗其眾，獲友仁。

translations.literal: Bin and Puxiang defeated their force and captured Youren.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Puxiang routed their army and took Youren prisoner.

sentences.zh: 友諒懼，約分界不相犯，乃釋友仁。

translations.literal: Youliang was afraid, agreed on a boundary and mutual non-aggression, and then released Youren.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang, alarmed, agreed to a boundary and a pledge of mutual non-aggression, and then freed Youren.

sentences.zh: 時江、楚諸郡皆為陳氏有，袁扼其要害，潭、岳、贛兵不得出。

translations.literal: At the time the commanderies of Jiang and Chu were all held by the Chen regime; Yuanzhou strangled their vital point, and troops from Tanzhou, Yuezhou, and Ganzhou could not break out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jiang and Chu commanderies were all in Chen hands; Yuanzhou sat athwart their lifeline, and the armies of Tanzhou, Yuezhou, and Ganzhou could not get out.

sentences.zh: 友諒勢大蹙。

translations.literal: Youliang's position was greatly constricted.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's situation grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵臨之，遂棄江州，彬力也。

translations.literal: When Taizu's army approached, he abandoned Jiangzhou—Bin's doing.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu's army drew near, he abandoned Jiangzhou—work largely of Bin's making.

sentences.zh: 太祖至龍興，令普祥仍守袁州，而以彬為江西行省參政。

translations.literal: When Taizu reached Longxing, he ordered Puxiang to continue holding Yuanzhou and made Bin provincial vice commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu arrived at Longxing, he left Puxiang to hold Yuanzhou and appointed Bin vice commissioner of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，普祥死，彬領其眾。

translations.literal: Before long Puxiang died and Bin took over his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Puxiang died, and Bin assumed command of his force.

sentences.zh: 普祥故殘暴，彬盡反所為，民甚安之。

translations.literal: Puxiang had been cruel and violent; Bin reversed everything he had done, and the people were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Puxiang had ruled with cruelty; Bin undid every harsh measure, and the people were deeply relieved.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春征贛州。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun in the campaign against Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang Yuchun in the campaign against Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 饒鼎臣據吉安，為熊天瑞聲援。

translations.literal: Rao Dingchen held Ji'an as a support for Xiong Tianrui.
translations.idiomatic: Rao Dingchen held Ji'an to support Xiong Tianrui.

sentences.zh: 遇春兵至，鼎臣走安福，彬以兵躡之。

translations.literal: When Yuchun's army arrived, Dingchen fled to Anfu and Bin pursued with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchun's army arrived, Dingchen fled to Anfu, and Bin pressed after him with troops.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣走茶陵，天瑞乃降。

translations.literal: Dingchen fled to Chaling and Tianrui then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen fled on to Chaling, and Tianrui then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 永新守將周安叛，彬從湯和執安，鼎臣亦殪。

translations.literal: The Yongxin garrison commander Zhou An rebelled; Bin followed Tang He in seizing An, and Dingchen was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou An, the Yongxin garrison commander, rebelled; Bin followed Tang He in capturing An, and Dingchen was slain as well.

sentences.zh: 移鎮袁州，招集諸山寨。

translations.literal: He shifted his garrison to Yuanzhou and gathered the various mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his garrison to Yuanzhou and brought the mountain stockades into submission.

sentences.zh: 江西悉定。

translations.literal: Jiangxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi was wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 進江淮行省中書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left chancellor of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封宜春侯，歲祿九百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yichun with an annual stipend of nine hundred piculs and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yichun with an annual stipend of nine hundred piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 四年，贛州上猶山寇叛，討平之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the bandits of Shangyou Mountain in Ganzhou rebelled; he campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the bandits of Shangyou Mountain in Ganzhou rose in revolt; he marched against them and put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 五年，古州等洞蠻叛，以鄧愈為征南將軍，三道出師，彬與營陽侯璟出澧州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the cave tribes of Guzhou and elsewhere rebelled; Deng Yu was made southern expedition general, and three columns marched out—Bin and Marquis of Yingyang Jing advanced from Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the cave tribes of Guzhou and other districts rebelled; Deng Yu was appointed southern expedition general, and three armies marched out—Bin and Yang Jing, Marquis of Yingyang, advanced from Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜第中都。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted a residence in Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was granted a mansion in Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 明年從徐達鎮北平，出練兵沂州、臨清。

translations.literal: The next year he followed Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping and went out to drill troops at Yizhou and Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping and went out to drill troops at Yizhou and Linqing.

sentences.zh: 二十三年坐胡惟庸黨死，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was executed as a member of the Hu Weiyong faction, and his title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was put to death on charges of belonging to Hu Weiyong's faction, and his marquisate was revoked.

sentences.zh: 葉升，合肥人。

translations.literal: Ye Sheng
translations.idiomatic: Ye Sheng

sentences.zh: 左君弼據廬，升自拔來歸。

translations.literal: Zuo Junbi held Lu; Sheng came out on his own initiative to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Junbi held Luzhou; Sheng broke away on his own and came over to the Ming cause.

sentences.zh: 以右翼元帥從征江州，以指揮僉事從取吳，以府軍衛指揮使從定明州。

translations.literal: As Right-wing Marshal he followed the campaign on Jiangzhou; as assistant commander he followed the seizure of Wu; as commander of the Prefectural Army Guard he followed the pacification of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Right-wing Marshal he took part in the campaign on Jiangzhou; as assistant commander he helped seize Wu; as commander of the Prefectural Army Guard he joined the pacification of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年論功，僉大都督府事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, when merits were weighed, he was made commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu, when honors were apportioned, he was made commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 明年從征西將軍湯和以舟師取蜀。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the western campaign general Tang He with the fleet to take Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed the western expedition general Tang He with the river fleet to conquer Shu.

sentences.zh: 越二年，出為都指揮使，鎮守西安，討平慶陽叛寇。

translations.literal: Two years later he went out as chief regional commander, garrisoned Xi'an, and campaigned to pacify rebel bandits in Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was posted as chief regional commander, garrisoned Xi'an, and marched to suppress the rebel bandits of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年復僉大都督府事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again served as commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again held office as commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 西番叛，與都督王弼征之，降乞失迦，平其部落。

translations.literal: When the western Tibetans rebelled, he joined Commissioner Wang Bi in the expedition, received the submission of Qieshijia, and pacified their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When the western tribes rebelled, he joined Commissioner Wang Bi on campaign, received the submission of Qieshijia, and pacified their clans.

sentences.zh: 復討平延安伯顏帖木兒，擒洮州番酋。

translations.literal: He again campaigned and pacified the Bole of Yan'an Bayan Temür, capturing the tribal chief of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again and subdued Bayan Temür, Bole of Yan'an, capturing the tribal chief of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 論功，封靖寧侯，歲祿二千石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingning with a stipend of two thousand piculs and hereditary commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingning with a stipend of two thousand piculs of grain and hereditary rank as commandant.

sentences.zh: 鎮遼東，修海、蓋、復三城。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Liaodong and repaired the three cities of Hai, Gaizhou, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Liaodong and rebuilt the three cities of Hai, Gaizhou, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 在鎮六年，邊備修舉，外寇不敢犯。

translations.literal: Six years in post; frontier defenses were maintained, and external raiders did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: For six years on the frontier he kept the defenses in order, and foreign raiders did not dare cross the border.

sentences.zh: 發高麗賂遺，帝屢賜敕，與唐勝宗同褒。

translations.literal: He exposed bribes from Goryeo; the Emperor repeatedly sent commendatory edicts, praising him together with Tang Shengzong.
translations.idiomatic: He reported bribes sent from Goryeo; the Emperor repeatedly issued commendatory edicts, praising him alongside Tang Shengzong.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命同普定侯陳桓總制諸軍於雲南定邊、姚安，立營、屯田，經理畢節衛。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was ordered, together with Marquis of Puding Chen Huan, to command all armies at Dingbian and Yao'an in Yunnan, establish camps and garrison farms, and administer the Bijie Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was ordered, together with Chen Huan, Marquis of Puding, to take overall command of the armies at Dingbian and Yao'an in Yunnan, establish camps and garrison farms, and administer the Bijie Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，東川、龍海諸蠻叛，升以參將從沐英討平之。

translations.literal: The next year the eastern Sichuan and Longhai tribes rebelled; Sheng as deputy general followed Mu Ying to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the tribes of eastern Sichuan and Longhai rebelled; Sheng served as deputy general under Mu Ying and put them down.

sentences.zh: 已而湖廣安福所千戶夏德忠誘九溪洞蠻為寇，升同胡海等討之。

translations.literal: Later the Anfu Company chiliarch Xia Dezhong of Huguang incited the Jiuxi cave tribes to raid; Sheng joined Hu Hai and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xia Dezhong, chiliarch of the Anfu Company in Huguang, incited the Jiuxi cave tribes to raid; Sheng joined Hu Hai and others in campaigning against them.

sentences.zh: 潛兵出賊後，掩擊，擒德忠。

translations.literal: He sent troops secretly behind the enemy, struck by surprise, and captured Dezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men secretly around behind the enemy, fell on them from the rear, and captured Dezhong.

sentences.zh: 立永定、九溪二衛，因留屯襄陽。

translations.literal: He established the Yongding and Jiuxi guards and remained to garrison at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Yongding and Jiuxi guards and stayed on to garrison Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 贛州山賊復結湖廣峒蠻為寇。

translations.literal: Mountain bandits of Ganzhou again joined the Dong tribes of Huguang in raiding.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain bandits of Ganzhou again joined forces with the Dong tribes of Huguang to raid.

sentences.zh: 升為副將軍，同胡海等討平之，俘獲萬七千人。

translations.literal: Sheng served as deputy general, joined Hu Hai and others in pacifying them, and took seventeen thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng served as deputy general, joined Hu Hai and others in suppressing them, and took seventeen thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 升凡三平叛蠻。

translations.literal: Sheng thrice pacified rebel tribes in all.
translations.idiomatic: In all, Sheng three times put down rebellious tribes.

sentences.zh: 再出練兵甘肅、河南。

translations.literal: He again went out to drill troops in Gansu and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He again went out to drill troops in Gansu and Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十五年八月，坐交通胡惟庸事覺，誅死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year his dealings with Hu Weiyong were exposed and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year his communications with Hu Weiyong came to light, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 涼國公藍玉，升姻也，玉敗，復連及升，以故名隸兩黨雲。

translations.literal: Duke of Liang Lan Yu was Sheng's in-law; when Yu fell, Sheng was implicated again—hence his name appears on both faction rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yu, Duke of Liang, was related to Sheng by marriage; when Yu fell, Sheng was implicated once more—hence his name is entered on the rolls of both factions.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：諸將當草昧之際，上觀天命，委心明主，戰勝攻取，克建殊勛，皆一時之智勇也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At a time when the realm was still unformed, these generals looked up to Heaven's mandate, entrusted themselves to the enlightened lord, fought and conquered, and each established extraordinary merit—all were men of timely wisdom and courage.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: In the days when the empire was still taking shape, these generals read Heaven's mandate in the signs above, gave their hearts to the enlightened sovereign, fought and conquered wherever they were sent, and each won a singular renown—they were, every one of them, the wise and the brave of their age.

sentences.zh: 及海內寧謐，乃名隸黨籍，或追論，或身坐，鮮有能自全者。

translations.literal: When the empire within the seas was tranquil, then their names were entered on faction registers—some pursued in retrospective judgment, some punished in person; few could preserve themselves intact.
translations.idiomatic: Once the land within the four seas was at peace, their names were entered on the rolls of faction instead—some pursued in judgment after the fact, some punished in their own persons; scarcely any kept themselves whole.

sentences.zh: 圭裳之錫固足酬功，而礪帶之盟不克再世，亦可慨矣夫。

translations.literal: The gift of robes and regalia was indeed ample reward for service, yet the covenant graven on the ring could not pass to a second generation—how lamentable indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The grant of court robes and regalia was reward enough for their service, yet the oath cut into the whetstone and girdle could not endure into a second generation—a thing to sigh over indeed.
